This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Iran pushes seven-day plan to end U.S. war in meetings with Qatari, Pakistani mediators: Iran is pushing a seven-day roadmap to end the war with the U.S., as Iranian officials held meetings with Qatari and Pakistani mediators on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York. The plan, which Tehran said was transmitted via mediators, calls for an end to hostilities on all fronts, including Gaza and Lebanon, the release of at least $12 billion in frozen Iranian assets, sanctions waivers for Iranian oil, an end to the U.S. naval blockade, and immediate nuclear talks. Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz on the seventh day. The proposal seeks to revive key provisions of the June U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding, which later collapsed amid mutual accusations of violations. A White House official told CNN that discussions through mediators were "positive and constructive," while another U.S. official told the New York Times that Washington would not rush into an agreement. Iran 's Pezeshkian says Tehran open to nuclear verification, agreement with U.S.: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian Tehran remains willing to reach an agreement with Washington and would accept international verification of its nuclear program and lower uranium enrichment levels, in an interview with Fox News. Asked whether Iran wants a nuclear bomb, Pezeshkian said, "Not at all," citing the late Supreme Leader's religious prohibition on weapons of mass destruction. "We are willing to dilute [enriched uranium] ... We are willing to submit ourselves to verification," he added. Pezeshkian said Iran still wants to move forward based on the previous agreement reached with the Trump administration. "If the current American government, within international legal frameworks, wishes to reach an agreement, fine," he said, adding that Tehran would not tie diplomacy to the timing of U.S. elections. Iran warns "flights for everyone or no one" as UAE, Iraq enforce U.S. aviation sanctions: The UAE all flights operated by Iranian airlines on Thursday, citing new U.S. sanctions threatening airports and aviation companies that continue servicing Iranian carriers. Iraq, Oman, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Turkmenistan have also imposed restrictions. Iran warned neighboring countries against enforcing the measures. Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei urged them not to join what he called the U.S. "adventure." "Flights in the region are either open to everyone or to no one," Supreme Leader adviser Mohammad Mokhber wrote in a on X. "If Iran is denied the ability to fly and receive airport services, no country in the region will have access to these facilities either." Yemen Saudi, Turkish, and Pakistani military chiefs to hold urgent talks on support for Riyadh: The military chiefs of Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan an urgent meeting to discuss support for Riyadh under the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, following Ansarallah attacks on Saudi cities and energy infrastructure. The countries' three foreign ministers met in New York on Thursday. The countries signed the agreement on August 7, stipulating that an armed attack against one would be considered an attack against all three. They have since begun establishing mechanisms to implement the pact, including a Saudi-based secretariat and expanded military cooperation. Pakistan said earlier this month that no military response to the Ansarallah attacks was then under discussion, while stressing it would fulfill its obligations if required. "When time comes, [we] will act under the agreement," Foreign Ministry spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said. France to send troops, radars, and defense systems to protect Saudi oil port: France soldiers, radars, and defense systems to Saudi Arabia to protect the Red Sea oil export hub of Yanbu following an Ansarallah attack, French President Emmanuel Macron said Thursday, according to Le Monde. Macron said the deployment was intended to protect the site, not involve French forces in the fighting. Yanbu, which handles several million barrels of oil a day, was "severely damaged" in the attacks, he said. Ansarallah claims attacks on Saudi military sites; government forces claim gains in Lahj: Yemen's Ansarallah said it attacked several Saudi military sites, including the Al-Tuwal area in Jizan and missile positions at Al-Dagharir camp on Friday. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed the attacks. Separately, Saudi-backed Yemeni forces claimed they captured the summit of Mount Numan and the Dar al-Kafir area in Lahj following an overnight operation. Ansarallah has not confirmed this. Palestine Israeli airstrike kills Palestinian, wounds others in Khan Younis: An Israeli airstrike a vehicle in the Mawasi area of Khan Younis on Friday, killing one Palestinian and wounding several others, according to WAFA. Israeli settlers attack Palestinians, torch vehicles: Nablus: Israeli settlers a group of Palestinian young men after stopping their vehicle in Beita's Al-Arma area, WAFA reported on Friday. Israeli forces separately raided Beita and detained a 17-year-old Palestinian boy from his home. Ramallah and Al-Bireh: Settlers Friday to three Palestinian vehicles in Rantis and spray-painted racist slogans on several homes. Across the occupied West Bank: There are now , gates, and other obstacles across the occupied West Bank, including 824 fixed closure points, increasingly restricting Palestinian movement, the Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission reported. Thirteen new fixed gates and checkpoints were documented over the past two months, including 10 in Jenin. Israeli police kill Palestinian man, bringing 2026 toll inside Israel to 10: Israeli police shot and killed a Palestinian man in his 30s in Yafa Al-Naseriyye, in northern Israel, Thursday night, bringing the documented number of Palestinians killed by police inside of Israel this year to 10. In most cases, victims' families and local groups disputed police accounts of the shootings. Previous investigations into Israeli police killings of Palestinian citizens have also been closed without charges against officers. UNRWA faces $100 million cashflow deficit amid Israeli attacks, U.S. funding cutoff: UNRWA is a $100 million cashflow deficit, forcing it to cut service hours by 20% and reduce salaries for local staff. The U.S., historically UNRWA's largest donor, has withheld funding since 2024. Israel has moved to dismantle the agency's operations in occupied East Jerusalem and restrict its work across the occupied Palestinian territory. In 2026, Israeli authorities demolished UNRWA's historic East Jerusalem headquarters, carried out an operation at its Kalandia vocational training center and forced the closure of its Old City health clinic. Nearly 400 UNRWA personnel have been killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza since October 2023. Abbas warns UN that Israeli policies threaten Palestinians ' "very existence": Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas, in prerecorded remarks after the U.S. denied visas to a Palestinian delegation for the second consecutive year, the UN General Assembly Thursday that Israeli policies now threaten Palestinians' "very life and existence," citing "killing, destruction, starvation, attempts at displacement, as well as a genocidal war that has created an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe." Abbas called Israeli activity in the West Bank a "malicious colonial plan" and urged the international community to implement a two-state solution based on international law. He also discussed the Palestinian Authority's plans to hold legislative elections on Nov. 28--the first since 2005-2006. Lebanon Israel launches airstrikes, shelling and incursions across southern Lebanon despite ceasefire: Nabatieh: Israeli warplanes two strikes within less than 15 minutes on the outskirts of Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah and another strike on Bani Hayyan on Friday, Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA) reported. An Israeli drone also struck between Kfar Tibnit and Nabatieh Al-Fawqa, while artillery shelling hit the outskirts of Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah, Mayfadoun, Nabatieh Al-Fawqa, and Kfar Tibnit. Marjayoun: Israeli forces to several homes in the Jallahiya area of Khiam. Hasbaya: Israeli forces the Sadana area outside Kfar Shouba, surrounded a farm where several shepherds were present and opened fire around it. Artillery shelling was also reported around Sadana and the outskirts of Hebbariyeh, alongside heavy machine-gun fire. " Lebanon wants to open a new page with Iran": Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, saying Lebanon wants to "open a new page" with Iran, establishing state-to-state relations, respect for sovereignty and non-interference, NNA reported. Salam said Lebanon "paid a heavy price" in its security, stability and economy and does not want to be an arena for regional conflicts. Salam also asked Iran to nominate a new ambassador to Beirut, nearly six months after Lebanon declared Tehran's former envoy persona non grata. The call for state-to-state relations comes amid Iran's longstanding political and military support of the Lebanese resistance group Hezbollah. Israel has continued attacks on Lebanon despite the signing of a U.S.-sponsored Framework Agreement on June 26 providing for a gradual Israeli withdrawal from occupied Lebanese territory in exchange for the disarmament of Hezbollah. U.S. News Netanyahu excoriates Mamdani, world leaders at UN amid Israel 's growing isolation: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu opened his UN General Assembly address Thursday by telling "any other moral cowards who haven't yet left this hall" to leave, as many attendees amid broad international condemnation of Israel's conduct in Gaza and the occupied West Bank. Netanyahu devoted a portion of his speech to New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani , calling him "antisemitic" and saying "shame on you for distorting the facts... shame on you for spitting in the face of truth." Mamdani called Netanyahu a "war criminal" earlier in the week. Netanyahu also rejected French President Emmanuel Macron 's Wednesday condemnation of daily Israeli "violations" in the West Bank as a "grotesque absurdity," highlighting the recent death of a French-Israeli citizen Netanyahu claimed came at the hands of Hamas. Nearly two dozen protesters, including Democratic nominee for Congress Darializa Avila Chevalier , whistleblower Chelsea Manning , and actor Hannah Einbinder , were arrested outside the UN on Thursday. Mortgage rates hit 7% for the first time since January 2025 as Iran war fallout hits housing market: The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate to 7.03% this week, up from 6.3% a year ago, Freddie Mac said Thursday, as war-driven energy costs and inflation push borrowing costs higher. Rates dipped below 6% in late February before climbing steadily after the U.S. and Israel launched attacks on Iran on Feb. 28. Existing home sales fell 2% in August to their lowest level since June 2025. Trump administration airs government-funded ad against socialism: A new 30-second Trump administration TV ad featuring President Donald Trump "communism, socialism, and Marxism" began airing Wednesday night on Fox News, Newsmax, and connected platforms, disclaiming it was "paid for by the U.S. government," according to ad tracker AdImpact. Sen. Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.) sent a letter to White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles demanding the ad's total cost, precise funding source, and purpose, saying it "raises deep concerns about the Trump Administration's use of taxpayer dollars" and potential violations of laws barring appropriated funds from promoting a political party. The White House called the spots "public service announcements" without addressing funding questions. Musician JMSN , whose song "Love Me" appears in the ad, said he did not authorize its use and is "looking for a lawyer." CNN, MS NOW, Politico reporters regain White House access despite delays; TV pool still suspended : CNN, MS NOW, and Politico journalists were to the White House around noon Thursday after a chaotic morning in which they were initially blocked despite an overnight order from Judge Timothy J. Kelly demanding their credentials be "immediately" restored. CNN's Betsy Klein saying she was turned away three times before being let in. The major networks' TV pool remained suspended. No print reporters were allowed into President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping 's meeting in the Oval Office and no network aired live footage. Senate narrowly fails to block Trump from ordering further Iran strikes : The Senate 49-50 against a war powers resolution that would have blocked President Donald Trump from ordering further strikes on Iran, with Republicans Rand Paul(Ky.), Susan Collins(Maine), Lisa Murkowski(Alaska), and Thom Tillis(N.C.) breaking from the party to vote yes alongside the Democrats; Democrat John Fetterman (Pa.) voted no, and Sen. Angela Alsobrooks(Md.) did not vote. Ten Democrats back Casar 's bill to ban superintelligence, pause advanced AI development: Ten House Democrats, Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Ro Khanna , are Rep. Greg Casar 's Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, which would prohibit AI "superintelligence" and pause advanced AI development until a vetting regime is established, with violators facing up to 20 years in prison. Khanna stressed the need for a verifiable pause and AI safety cooperation with China. Energy Secretary Wright pushes industry for voluntary diesel export cuts amid antitrust concerns : Energy Secretary Chris Wright oil industry executives to voluntarily reduce diesel exports and boost domestic inventories, telling reporters in Allentown, Pennsylvania, "let's push prices down." The comments follow a Politico report that the White House was weighing a 90-day mandatory export ban that drew industry pushback. Energy executives working with White House officials warned that coordinating voluntary export reductions among companies could violate federal antitrust laws. Diesel prices have hit record highs amid supply disruptions from the Iran war and Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries, with U.S. exports up more than 12% since the war began and domestic inventories running 12% below the five-year average. Massachusetts to investigate DraftKings ' use of AI after NYT report on targeting losing gamblers: The Massachusetts Gaming Commission Thursday it will examine how DraftKings and other betting companies use AI, following a New York Times investigation that found DraftKings used machine learning to identify losing gamblers most likely to keep betting when sent promotional offers. Massachusetts prohibits using automated systems "known or reasonably expected" to make gambling more addictive. DraftKings denied using AI "to target anyone based on losses" or market based on "indicators of potential problem gaming." Federal lawmakers, including Sen. Richard Blumenthal(D-Conn), have proposed a nationwide ban on AI-driven targeted gambling promotions in response to the Times' reporting, Trump administration asks Supreme Court to revive third-country deportation policy : The Justice Department an emergency request Thursday asking the Supreme Court to pause a lower court order requiring immigration officials to give deportees notice and a chance to challenge removal before sending them to "third countries" where they have no ties. Last week, an appellate court largely upheld the ruling and DHS was forced to cancel a flight carrying 70 would-be deportees to three countries. Solicitor General D. John Sauer wrote that the policy had enabled removal of "thousands" of people, including "some of the worst of the worst criminal aliens," and warned the lower court's ruling "undermines our standing abroad" by disrupting diplomatic arrangements with receiving nations. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson gave lawyers challenging the policy until Monday to respond. Federal judge rules ICE 's NYC detention conditions "inhumane and unconstitutional," orders sweeping fixes: U.S. District Judge Lewis A. Kaplan a permanent injunction against ICE over conditions at the 26 Federal Plaza detention facility in New York City, writing in a 127-page opinion that officials "intentionally concealed or recklessly disregarded the truth" about compliance with his earlier orders and that ICE "objectively deprived detainees of sleep, sanitary living conditions, basic personal hygiene needs, sufficient food and water, and adequate medical care" by holding people far longer than the facility's intended 12-hour limit. Kaplan found detainees were also "severely restricted" from meaningfully accessing counsel, with phone calls limited to a few minutes and often overheard by ICE staff, calling the agency's disregard of prior capacity limits "persistent, egregious, and, at a minimum, reckless, if not willful." The injunction requires ICE to provide at least 50 square feet of floor space per person, temperatures between 68 and 74 degrees, three daily meals, hygiene supplies, bedding for overnight detainees, an on-site medical professional at all times, and confidential attorney phone access. GAO finds ICE wasted millions in rushed detention expansion push: A Government Accountability Office report Thursday found ICE "wasted funds on unsuccessful detention initiatives" by launching new expansion efforts without a strategic plan, including spending nearly $3 million assembling tents at Guantanamo Bay that were never used and more than $20 million on "non-recoverable costs" for warehouses it purchased last year and now intends to sell. The report also found ICE is reimbursing Florida at 171% above the median rate for running "Alligator Alcatraz" and another detention facility. California Supreme Court orders Riverside sheriff to return 650,000 illegally seized ballots : The California Supreme Court Thursday unanimously that Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco unlawfully seized about 650,000 ballots from California's 2025 special election as part of a fraud investigation state officials said had no basis, ordering their return. Associate Justice Goodwin H. Liu wrote that the seizure involved "over 1,000 boxes of documents... the most precious documents of the citizenry in a democracy: their votes." The investigation targeted a special election in which voters approved Proposition 50, a Democratic-backed congressional redistricting plan responding to Texas's own gerrymander. Bianco launched the probe when he was a Republican candidate for governor. NSA spending billions to test AI models, exceeding prior estimates for federal oversight : The National Security Agency is billions of dollars this year evaluating frontier AI models through its Artificial Intelligence Security Center, according to two sources familiar with classified intelligence estimates, a figure far exceeding earlier congressional projections of just $20 million, according to The Washington Sun. Pentagon investigates how F-35 parts diverted to Hong Kong: The Pentagon on Thursday that it is investigating how a shipment of F-35 fighter jet parts, in transit from Australia for repair, was diverted to Hong Kong, with a defense official saying it is "actively working with U.S. authorities and industry partners to retrieve these components." Bloomberg News reported the parts are now in China's possession, though the Pentagon declined to confirm this. The missing components reportedly relate to the F-35's canopy and weapons bay door, which, while lacking advanced avionics, could still reveal information about the plane's radar-absorbent stealth coating. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Nepal PM Shah warns UN that deadly floods are "a warning to the world" on climate change: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah the UN General Assembly Thursday that August floods that killed at least 1,453 people, with 5,500 still missing, were "not just a local tragedy," asking leaders if they had "really heard that warning" in reference to the rising threat of climate change. Shah noted Nepal contributes less than one-tenth of 1% of global heat-trapping emissions yet "our glaciers are retreating, our mountain slopes are becoming unstable... every major disaster threatens to erase years of development." Nepal has requested the maximum $20 million from the UN's loss and damage fund--a fraction of the disaster's estimated $5 billion cost. The U.S. pledged an additional $31 million in flood recovery support earlier this week. U.S. arranges new trilateral Ukraine-Russia talks, possibly in UAE; Trump approves Patriot production : The U.S. is working to new trilateral peace talks between Ukraine and Russia at a technical level, with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy saying Washington has proposed the United Arab Emirates as a possible location, while the Kremlin confirmed a meeting could happen soon. Zelenskyy also said Trump has agreed to let Ukraine produce advanced Patriot air defense missiles domestically, though any licensed production would take more than a year to come online. Argentina 's poverty rate climbs to 32.3% as Milei's economic momentum stalls: Argentina's poverty rate to 32.3% in the first half of 2026, up from 28.2% the previous half-year, according to an official report. Extreme poverty rose from 6.3% to 7.5%, with roughly 9.7 million people across surveyed urban areas living below the poverty line, including nearly 45% of children under 15. Formal private-sector employment has fallen for 13 consecutive months. As president, Javier Milei has pursued a rigid austerity program, slashing public spending and tightening the country's monetary policy. At least 41 dead after boat capsizes on Lake Tanganyika in DRC : A boat carrying roughly 100 people and cargo near the Congolese village of Mapera on Lake Tanganyika Thursday, killing at least 41 people and prompting ongoing search operations for remaining passengers, the Associated Press reports; 49 people have been rescued so far. The vessel, traveling from Kigoma, Tanzania, to Kalemie, DRC, reportedly began tilting around 1 a.m. as passengers slept, a survivor told Radio Okapi. The cause remains unclear. On August 28, a fire and explosion aboard the MV Pacifique on the same route killed six crew members. Costa Rica 's president fires foreign minister after unauthorized attendance of Trump security summit: Costa Rica President Laura Fernandez Foreign Minister Manuel Tovar effective immediately Thursday after he attended a Tuesday meeting of the Shield of the Americas--a U.S.-led anti-cartel coalition launched by the Trump administration in March--without notifying her, preventing her from participating herself. The government said Tovar's negligence "caused significant strategic damage," calling the coalition, which several right-wing Latin American presidents also attended, "fundamental to its national and public security policy." U.S.-sanctioned tanker Sibu 1 freed from Somali pirates in Puntland operation : Puntland's maritime police that the force had freed the U.S.-sanctioned oil tanker Sibu 1 during a counter-piracy operation, with commander Mohamed Jama telling Reuters "the ship is free and the pirates are all in the hands of our forces." The Eritrea-flagged tanker, seized by six armed individuals on August 20, had been sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury in December for allegedly forming part of a "shadow fleet" helping Iranian petroleum products evade U.S. sanctions. Sibu 1 was at least the 13th vessel attacked off Somalia or in the Gulf of Aden this year, according to International Maritime Bureau and UKMTO data. UNHCR reports 20-fold surge in Sudanese refugees fleeing to Chad amid funding shortfall : Over 55,000 Sudanese refugees have escaped into eastern Chad since January, fueled by ongoing violence and growing instability, according to the UNHCR. More than 400 people a day have crossed from Sudan into eastern Chad over the past week--a 20-fold increase from recent months--as fighting between Sudan's army and the Rapid Support Forces intensifies across Darfur, Kordofan and Blue Nile, the UN refugee agency said. UN Regional Refugee Coordinator Mamadou Dian Balde said arrivals describe fleeing "aerial bombardments" and "drone attacks." Balde also discussed the UNHCR's funding shortfall, with the agency receiving only 18% of the $1.6 billion it needs this year. He noted that the change means "less food ... less capacity for people to be relocated to safer areas ... less capacity to shelter themselves." The UNHCR also warned that unmet needs in Chad could push more Sudanese refugees toward attempting dangerous onward journeys to Europe, as the more than three-year civil war has displaced up to 14 million people overall, with nearly 1 million refugees having crossed into Chad since the conflict began. TPLF fighters in Ethiopia take over airport as "full-blown war" resumes in Amhara: Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) fighters have captured the Alula Aba Nega Airport in Mekelle, the capital of Ethiopia's Tigray region, amidst fresh fighting with federal troops. Ethiopia's National Defense Force also said on Friday it at least 272 Tigray People's Liberation Front fighters and wounded 260 more in a counter-offensive after TPLF and allied forces attacked several areas of North Wollo in Amhara region. A civil aviation official at the airport, Tulu Ayenew, said on Friday that since Wednesday TPLF and government forces were fighting near the airport but eventually TPLF overpowered their opponents and are currently in full control. TPLF Vice President Amanuel Assefa told AFP, "We are in the situation of full-blown war now," confirming Tigrayan forces are fighting alongside local groups in Afar and Amhara. The escalation has disrupted air travel after Tigrayan forces seized three local airports, forcing the suspension of flights to the UNESCO-listed site of Lalibela. Registration, early voting, voting by mail, and Election Day — here are the key dates to know.
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139946808/649032690/-1405467182?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3NTU2YmFhNS1mNmI4LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=iYC7AC1OAv4T86aZ07geNRHWo_KEeeV6_U0-vHiCg9E=&emci=89cdcf9e-58b8-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=7556baa5-f6b8-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=14565883)

| | Welcome back to Fact Friday. **Today, I want to make sure you have the key dates and deadlines you need to make your voting plan for November 3.** Election Day will be here before we know it, so mark your calendar and save these dates:
* **Monday, October 5:** Last day to register to vote

* **Monday, October 19:** Early voting begins

* **Friday, October 23:** Deadline to apply for a ballot by mail

* **Friday, October 30:** Last day of early voting

* **Tuesday, November 3:** ELECTION DAY!

**If you still need to register — or want to make sure your voter registration is up to date — now is the time to check.** [CHECK YOUR REGISTRATION](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139946809/649032691/-1312914512?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3NTU2YmFhNS1mNmI4LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=iYC7AC1OAv4T86aZ07geNRHWo_KEeeV6_U0-vHiCg9E=&emci=89cdcf9e-58b8-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=7556baa5-f6b8-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=14565883) **If you plan to vote early, you can cast your ballot at any Early Voting Location in El Paso County. I encourage you to vote early if you can!** [EARLY VOTING LOCATIONS](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139946810/649032692/-571584443?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3NTU2YmFhNS1mNmI4LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=iYC7AC1OAv4T86aZ07geNRHWo_KEeeV6_U0-vHiCg9E=&emci=89cdcf9e-58b8-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=7556baa5-f6b8-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=14565883) If you are eligible and plan to vote by mail, [**your application must be received — not just postmarked — by October 23.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139946811/649032693/-681798009?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3NTU2YmFhNS1mNmI4LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=iYC7AC1OAv4T86aZ07geNRHWo_KEeeV6_U0-vHiCg9E=&emci=89cdcf9e-58b8-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=7556baa5-f6b8-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=14565883) Don't wait to send your ballot back. If your ballot is not postmarked, it must be received by**7 p.m. on Election Day.** If it is properly postmarked by Election Day, it must be received **b** y**5 p.m. the following day.** On Election Day, you can cast your ballot at any Vote Center in El Paso County, and **polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.** [ELECTION DAY VOTING](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139946812/649032694/-928885128?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3NTU2YmFhNS1mNmI4LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=iYC7AC1OAv4T86aZ07geNRHWo_KEeeV6_U0-vHiCg9E=&emci=89cdcf9e-58b8-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=7556baa5-f6b8-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=14565883) **Whether you vote early, by mail if eligible, or on Election Day, the important thing is to make your plan now.****Decide when you're going to vote, know where you need to go, and make sure you're ready before the day arrives.** If you want to keep getting clear, fact-based breakdowns of the issues affecting our community, make sure you stay connected and share this with someone who should be paying attention, too. clean_body: Registration, early voting, voting by mail, and Election Day — here are the key dates to know. | | | | Welcome back to Fact Friday. Today, I want to make sure you have the key dates and deadlines you need to make your voting plan for November 3. Election Day will be here before we know it, so mark your calendar and save these dates: Monday, October 5: Last day to register to vote Monday, October 19: Early voting begins Friday, October 23: Deadline to apply for a ballot by mail Friday, October 30: Last day of early voting Tuesday, November 3: ELECTION DAY! If you still need to register — or want to make sure your voter registration is up to date — now is the time to check. If you plan to vote early, you can cast your ballot at any Early Voting Location in El Paso County. I encourage you to vote early if you can! If you are eligible and plan to vote by mail, Don't wait to send your ballot back. If your ballot is not postmarked, it must be received by7 p.m. on Election Day. If it is properly postmarked by Election Day, it must be received b y5 p.m. the following day. On Election Day, you can cast your ballot at any Vote Center in El Paso County, and polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Whether you vote early, by mail if eligible, or on Election Day, the important thing is to make your plan now.**Decide when you're going to vote, know where you need to go, and make sure you're ready before the day arrives. If you want to keep getting clear, fact-based breakdowns of the issues affecting our community, make sure you stay connected and share this with someone who should be paying attention, too. Staying informed is power. Let's use it, El Paso. name: Roy Cooper
subject: Why not me? Why not you?
body:
Fair warning: This is going to be a long story.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1413&source=&t=1&akid=3831%2E124072%2ElXq4en) | | | |
---
Peter,
With your support, I plan to get to the Senate in January with one guiding principle: fighting for North Carolinians, who have repeatedly put their trust in me to do what's right for our state.
That said, joining the race was not an easy decision to make. So I want to backtrack a bit and tell you how we got here today.
(Fair warning, though: This is going to be a long story. [**_So if you’re short on time, please consider chipping in to my grassroots campaign before you click away._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1413&amount=5&t=8&akid=3831%2E124072%2ElXq4en))
**_How we got here:_**
I had planned on serving North Carolina from here at home. Serving as Governor was one of the great honors of my life, but after two terms, I was ready to hang up my suit and tie and exchange my dress shoes for my new and more comfortable Jordans.
That being said, our nation cannot afford two more years of unchecked GOP rule in Washington DC. The attacks – on health care, on our democratic values and even on Americans – have to stop. **So this race was too consequential to sit out. The stakes are simply too high.**
Leaders should strengthen their communities by putting the needs of working folks over the wealthy few. So whether it was adding thousands of jobs, giving school teachers a much-needed raise or expanding access to Medicaid, my #1 priority over my eight years as Governor was to improve the lives of everyday North Carolinians. Together, we did that.
**This is the work I’m ready to continue as the next U.S. Senator from North Carolina** – but it’s going to take flipping our seat blue for the first time in a generation. Easier said than done.
**_How it’s going:_**
While I didn’t plan to go to Washington DC, I couldn’t stand by and watch the GOP rip away health care access, gut funding for public schools and chip away at the middle class. They’re not making this country "great again." In fact, they’re hurting it.
So I had to get back in the fight, and I’m so glad I did.
Since launching this campaign, hundreds of thousands of folks like you have joined our grassroots movement for change, and momentum is on our side. **The hard part will be maintaining it for the last month-and-a-half until Election Day.**
I might be undefeated (6-0) in statewide races, but this is hands-down the most competitive race of my career. North Carolina is the best pick-up opportunity for Democrats this cycle, and taking back the Senate hinges on us winning. That’s why President Trump came to Gastonia last week to rally alongside Michael Whatley, why JD Vance came back to NC for more this past Monday and why outside groups are spending more than $100 million on attack ads to defeat me.
**In light of two recent polls of likely voters, the surge of dark money on the airwaves and in-state MAGA attacks is taking a toll on our slim lead.**
That said, I’m a prisoner of hope – and if there’s a silver lining, it’s that the attacks from Whatley, the President and their super PAC allies are their own vote of confidence, in a way. They wouldn’t be coming after us so hard if they weren’t terrified of the grassroots momentum we’re building. **That’s how I know we really can win this thing.**
**_What’s next?_**
Now, I won’t pretend it’s going to be easy. Things worth fighting for rarely are.
The next 39 days will be all gas, no brakes – and if there’s one thing I’ve learned over a career of running tough races, it’s that it takes _a lot_ of resources (and winning will take even more).
We can fight back and flip North Carolina’s seat blue, but we’re going to have to work harder than ever, and it will take all of us doing our part. Just as in elections past, I can’t do this alone.
[**_So if you’re able, Peter, I’m hoping you’ll chip in $5, or whatever you can, to help me flip this seat, retake the Senate for Democrats and return power in Washington DC to the hands of working families._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1413&amount=5&t=9&akid=3831%2E124072%2ElXq4en)

I was going to start this email like this: _Every other day there’s a new, jaw-dropping article about something awful the Trump administration is doing._ But that would be blatantly untrue, because it’s WAY more than every other day. The pace at which this President and his administration are doing insane, reckless, cruel, and often _illegal_ things is one of the most overwhelming parts of the situation we’re in right now. This isn’t new — Steve Bannon told us nearly a decade ago that “flooding the zone” is central to the MAGA strategy. And it’s working. Trump has signed 284 Executive Orders since returning to the White House, on everything from birthright citizenship to abortion to tariffs to fossil fuels. Combine that with how he’s swept formerly independent agencies under presidential purview and packed the courts with right-wing allies, and it becomes increasingly clear that he aspires to rule in the style of the foreign dictators he so admires. There’s one missing piece of the puzzle, though. We may not be able to count on the judicial system to fully keep Trump in check, but there’s a whole third branch of government whose job it is to serve as a check on executive power... CONGRESS!! Yes, the good old U.S. Congress, a governing body that is quite literally _required_ by the Constitution to conduct oversight and balance out presidential overreach, but somehow finds itself wholly incapable of lifting a finger in service of that oath. I say “somehow,” but we know exactly how: Mike Johnson and his fellow House Republicans are simply too afraid of Donald Trump — too obsessed with pleasing him in an attempt to prevent a temper tantrum — to do their jobs. OK, that was my rant. But because I’m aware that you didn’t sign up for these emails just to listen to me vent, let me offer a way out of this mess: Win in November. And not just by a little bit (because as we know, Trump is poised to claim fraud and use any excuse to sow misinformation about our elections). By A LOT. By so much that the will of the American people is unmistakable: we want a functioning government, we want a stable democracy, and we want our elected officials to do their damn jobs. I am optimistic about our chances at doing just that, but I think we all know from past elections that the _worst possible thing_ to do when you think you’re winning is to become complacent. Complacency is the enemy of action — and action is the antidote to ALL of this. So today I ask you to join me in taking action. If you’re in a position financially to donate, one concrete action you can do right this second is chip in to my re-election campaign. Your contributions help me keep this seat blue (which is of course very important!), but they also help me support the Democrats in tough races around the country — both incumbents and challengers — who really need more resources. Please consider donating to support our efforts today, ahead of our 9/30 FEC filing deadline (which is another thing that is very important!). Here’s the link: **[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139949014/649040485/-642992695?refcode=260925em_sjj_trumprant&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiZTUzZDIyOS1mYWI4LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=FOyypI06cg9vrkSS6Ad5ac2olCRJEdWo0oCk3-0aVhQ=)** If you can’t afford to donate, I completely understand, and I hope you know that I don’t expect you to give when it’s not financially feasible. I’m glad you’re on this team, and I hope you’ll keep reading these updates either way. Thank you for everything. With you,
Sara

Hey folks,
This one gets ugly fast. We're breaking down the increasingly desperate campaign around Andrew and Tristan Tate, the claims being made about their detention, and the attempt by their supporters to turn Jeffrey Epstein into a defense of the brothers.
And yeah, there's a lot to unpack here.
* [**00:01:37**] The Tate media machine pushes dramatic claims about "solitary confinement," and I break down what we actually know from the material discussed in this episode.
* [**00:03:44**] Their lawyer jumps into the PR fight, trying to connect an unrelated solitary-confinement case to the Tates as their supporters search for sympathy.
* [**00:05:50**] The Epstein argument takes center stage and we look at past posts attributed to Andrew Tate that make this new line of defense especially striking.
* [**00:08:03**] A photo of Tate-world influencers opens up the bigger conversation about the Manosphere, young men, Trump, and the political promises these figures sold their audiences.
* [**00:10:03**] The legal and political strategy appears to be hitting a wall as the episode examines why the people the Tates have publicly appealed to aren't stepping in.

This episode is about more than Andrew and Tristan Tate. It's about the ecosystem surrounding them: the influencers, lawyers, political connections, social-media propaganda, and audience that helped give this movement power in the first place. And it's about why accountability matters even when powerful people elsewhere have escaped it. ## **A Missed Step, a Broken Ankle, and a Very Forced Lesson in Patience**
If you watched the show this week, you might have noticed I was broadcasting from a slightly different setup - or maybe you just wondered where I've been over the last few days.
Last Saturday night, I was walking down a flight of outdoor stairs heading from a neighbor's house to my daughter's soccer game. I missed a single step. In a split second, my right ankle went one direction, my left leg and tendons went another, and my weekend plans were instantly replaced with a trip to the emergency room. By Friday, I was in the operating room undergoing surgery.
[| | | | | Sean Spicer

The reality of the diagnosis? For the next few months - yes, you read that right, _months_ \- my left leg is going to be locked in a full brace.
For a guy who is used to moving at 100 miles an hour and traveling non-stop, being forced to slow down is a massive reality check. Simple daily tasks are suddenly major logistics operations, and my reliance on the people around me is going to reach levels that are, frankly, pretty challenging for a fiercely independent person.
Lying in bed recovering gives you a lot of time to reflect. As I've been sitting here, I've come away with a few hard personal rules and post-recovery resolutions - starting with one major bad habit we all fall into: **procrastination.**

Grassroots supporters like you are the engine of this movement. The MAGA

up for working families.

Alexandria, Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida have shown what real leadership
looks like. In Congress, they're the fiercest champions for accessible
healthcare, reproductive freedom, worker protections, affordable housing,
and climate action — fighting every day for the communities that need them
the most.

Because the Squad refuses to bend to corporate PACs, special interests, or
Trump's authoritarianism, outside forces will do anything to unseat them
and silence our movement for progressive change.

With the midterms less than six weeks away, everyone will be watching next

Dear Friend, Earlier this month, over 100 state lawmakers from our 15 state freedom caucuses along with over 150 more supporters and grassroots allies came to Grapevine, Texas for our **3rd Annual State Freedom Caucus Summit**. They came to strategize, to compare notes on the fights back home, and to be recognized for what they pulled off this past year. Our friend OMB Director Russ Vought headlined our Friday night dinner, introduced by House Freedom Caucus hero, Congressman Chip Roy.
---
---
_House Freedom Caucus's Congressman Chip Roy_
---
---
_OMB Director Russ Vought_
---
|
---
**THE AWARDS DINNER** Then came Saturday night and the Awards Dinner, emceed by long time conservative movement leader Tom McClusky. Keith Olbermann once named Tom the "Worst Person in the World," which tells you everything you need to know about him.We handed out nine awards. Here are the winners!**⚡️Pettiest Punishment Award⚡️** **Maryland Freedom Caucus Delegates Mark Fisher and Brian Chisholm.** In today's Maryland, calling a communist a communist gets you an ethics charge. Democrat leadership filed one against them, then hired a Democrat campaign donor as the lawyer. With the help from our friends at the Oversight Project, Mark and Brian are not backing down.**⚡️Best In-Session Fight Award⚡️****The South Carolina Freedom Caucus** , for gutting a bloated tax hike that the establishment had dressed up as "roads reform." The caucus worked the grassroots, tipped off county council members that they would be stuck passing the local tax increases, and watched the pressure do its work. The final bill was rewritten on the floor using language from SCFC member Rep. Joe White's Facebook post. A GOP caucus member even admitted it out loud.**⚡️Best Out-of-Session Fight Award⚡️****The Wyoming Freedom Caucus.** The Weston County Clerk botched the 2024 election in her county and then ignored a subpoena from the Audit Committee, led by WYFC members Chris Knapp and Rachel Rodriguez-Williams. The sheriff arrested her. She pled guilty to a misdemeanor. She is not the county clerk anymore.**⚡️Rookie of the Year Award⚡️****Minnesota Freedom Caucus State Senator Michael Holmstrom.** A freshman who was as comfortable taking on Minnesota's regime media as he was on the Senate floor. Remember his name. His future is bright.
---
---
Minnesota State Senator Michael Holmstrom
---
**⚡️Best Communications Award⚡️**
**
The Montana Freedom Caucus** won for their relentless exposure of the liberal Republicans and Democrats who pushed through a property tax hike, a bloated state budget, and more.**⚡️Best Floor Speech Award⚡️**
**
Illinois Freedom Caucus's Chris Miller** , on Illinois Democrats clinging to the same stupid ideas that are destroying their state.Watch it here:

[](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjkE6fRekQpv4SixOLna3V69Nx30idU2hvG7q3L4ZCor90vvT4BkH3y8spzu9bna67w-3D-3DiKDt_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerHqopsVebnu8-2BIe-2FXIcqZx22w0uIQYkNLlACGrCSJCVAzd1OPsKpGYzbpF80e-2FfhdyP7hqTxWGTM7CKMBGQAgaexlfzoQNFic8WQhCEa8HswbjZNBujTnqyLZt67X-2By5xSlILiS4fGLLv3NYrPChmcQJFebp7yjh-2FbNV80OtOX0F1b0v5u-2FD3wYTjrlCn-2Fq4aAvzrVcuS-2FawCLyv9ab7Pw3S9Ueh9FEw4l74aWpNr-2BOM-3D)
---
|
---
**⚡️Best State Director Award⚡️** **Maryland's Ali Rak.** Our state directors read every bill, run the caucus meetings, wrangle the coalition partners, and do a dozen other things nobody sees. They do not do it for the paycheck, but for the love of freedom and saving their state. Ali Rak set the standard this year.Which brings us to the last two awards of the night, and the reason this email has a theme. **⚡️Best State Lawmaker Award⚡️****Missouri Freedom Caucus Chairman Nick Schroer.** The Missouri Freedom Caucus needed a jolt after losing several long-serving members and taking on a wave of new ones in 2025. Nick was the jolt. He led his team on many successful policy fights and educated the public about them. And he did all of it while co-hosting our radio show, _State Freedom Caucus Unfiltered_ , which has become the place our lawmakers go to get their fights in front of a national audience. Nick is a stone cold outlaw conservative if there ever was one.
---
---
_Missouri State Senator Nick Schroer_
---
**⚡️Best State Freedom Caucus Award⚡️**
**
The Missouri Freedom Caucus** This is the one award to rule them all, and it is not a participation trophy. It goes to the caucus that acts like an infantry unit. They vote together, plan together, defend each other, pray together, and are very public about their intentions. Under Nick's chairmanship, Missouri had a ridiculous year. They cut **$4 BILLION** out of the state budget. Not a slowdown in the growth of spending. An actual cut. They single-handedly led the charge on passing the 7-1 redistricting map. They legalized over-the-counter ivermectin. They passed the Born Alive Abortion Survivors Act. And the entire state knows it because they continually remind the voters who the good guys and the bad guys are in Jefferson City. The two biggest awards of the night. Both went to Missouri. The Show Me State is in good hands with the Missouri Freedom Caucus.
---
---
_Missouri Freedom Caucus members, along with Missouri state director, Tim Jones, receiving the Best State Freedom Caucus award._

|

**WE NEED YOUR HELP TO KEEP THE MOMENTUM** Every one of these awards represents a year of work by people who could have taken the easy road and did not. That is what your support pays for.The 2027 sessions are already coming, and the other side never stops. If you want more nights like this one, you can pitch in right here.

clean_body: | | | | | Dear Friend, Earlier this month, over 100 state lawmakers from our 15 state freedom caucuses along with over 150 more supporters and grassroots allies came to Grapevine, Texas for our 3rd Annual State Freedom Caucus Summit. They came to strategize, to compare notes on the fights back home, and to be recognized for what they pulled off this past year. Our friend OMB Director Russ Vought headlined our Friday night dinner, introduced by House Freedom Caucus hero, Congressman Chip Roy. House Freedom Caucus's Congressman Chip Roy OMB Director Russ Vought | THE AWARDS DINNER Then came Saturday night and the Awards Dinner, emceed by long time conservative movement leader Tom McClusky. Keith Olbermann once named Tom the "Worst Person in the World," which tells you everything you need to know about him.We handed out nine awards. Here are the winners!⚡️Pettiest Punishment Award⚡️ Maryland Freedom Caucus Delegates Mark Fisher and Brian Chisholm. In today's Maryland, calling a communist a communist gets you an ethics charge. Democrat leadership filed one against them, then hired a Democrat campaign donor as the lawyer. With the help from our friends at the Oversight Project, Mark and Brian are not backing down.⚡️Best In-Session Fight Award⚡️The South Carolina Freedom Caucus , for gutting a bloated tax hike that the establishment had dressed up as "roads reform." The caucus worked the grassroots, tipped off county council members that they would be stuck passing the local tax increases, and watched the pressure do its work. The final bill was rewritten on the floor using language from SCFC member Rep. Joe White's Facebook post. A GOP caucus member even admitted it out loud.⚡️Best Out-of-Session Fight Award⚡️The Wyoming Freedom Caucus. The Weston County Clerk botched the 2024 election in her county and then ignored a subpoena from the Audit Committee, led by WYFC members Chris Knapp and Rachel Rodriguez-Williams. The sheriff arrested her. She pled guilty to a misdemeanor. She is not the county clerk anymore.⚡️Rookie of the Year Award⚡️Minnesota Freedom Caucus State Senator Michael Holmstrom. A freshman who was as comfortable taking on Minnesota's regime media as he was on the Senate floor. Remember his name. His future is bright. Minnesota State Senator Michael Holmstrom ⚡️Best Communications Award⚡️ The Montana Freedom Caucus won for their relentless exposure of the liberal Republicans and Democrats who pushed through a property tax hike, a bloated state budget, and more.⚡️Best Floor Speech Award⚡️ Illinois Freedom Caucus's Chris Miller , on Illinois Democrats clinging to the same stupid ideas that are destroying their state.Watch it here: | ⚡️Best State Director Award⚡️ Maryland's Ali Rak. Our state directors read every bill, run the caucus meetings, wrangle the coalition partners, and do a dozen other things nobody sees. They do not do it for the paycheck, but for the love of freedom and saving their state. Ali Rak set the standard this year.Which brings us to the last two awards of the night, and the reason this email has a theme. ⚡️Best State Lawmaker Award⚡️Missouri Freedom Caucus Chairman Nick Schroer. The Missouri Freedom Caucus needed a jolt after losing several long-serving members and taking on a wave of new ones in 2025. Nick was the jolt. He led his team on many successful policy fights and educated the public about them. And he did all of it while co-hosting our radio show, State Freedom Caucus Unfiltered , which has become the place our lawmakers go to get their fights in front of a national audience. Nick is a stone cold outlaw conservative if there ever was one. Missouri State Senator Nick Schroer ⚡️Best State Freedom Caucus Award⚡️ The Missouri Freedom Caucus This is the one award to rule them all, and it is not a participation trophy. It goes to the caucus that acts like an infantry unit. They vote together, plan together, defend each other, pray together, and are very public about their intentions. Under Nick's chairmanship, Missouri had a ridiculous year. They cut $4 BILLION out of the state budget. Not a slowdown in the growth of spending. An actual cut. They single-handedly led the charge on passing the 7-1 redistricting map. They legalized over-the-counter ivermectin. They passed the Born Alive Abortion Survivors Act. And the entire state knows it because they continually remind the voters who the good guys and the bad guys are in Jefferson City. The two biggest awards of the night. Both went to Missouri. The Show Me State is in good hands with the Missouri Freedom Caucus. Missouri Freedom Caucus members, along with Missouri state director, Tim Jones, receiving the Best State Freedom Caucus award. | WE NEED YOUR HELP TO KEEP THE MOMENTUM Every one of these awards represents a year of work by people who could have taken the easy road and did not. That is what your support pays for.The 2027 sessions are already coming, and the other side never stops. If you want more nights like this one, you can pitch in right here. We'll be back with another update soon. Until then, please be sure to our efforts so that we can support our State Freedom Caucuses!In Liberty, Andy RothPresidentState Freedom Caucus Network | |

In Milwaukee County, I’ve seen first-hand how working families thrive when we invest in healthcare, affordable housing, public education, mental health services, and public transit.
**But while we’ve been fighting for working families, my Trump-backed, MAGA opponent Tom Tiffany has a _very_ different focus.**
→ He's championed some of the most restrictive abortion policies in the country.
→ He’s an election denier who voted against certifying the 2020 election.

We're not going to beat around the bush: today's Supreme Court ruling is terrible news for the midterm election.
In another 6-3 vote along ideological lines, the Court gave Trump the green light to use his own database to help sympathetic red states "hunt" for noncitizen and ineligible voters, an exceedingly rare occurrence that is at the heart of MAGA's false claims about the 2020 election.
The new system takes in citizenship information, Social Security numbers, and other sensitive data about millions of Americans without their permission to build out a deeply flawed database to serve as a launching pad for Trump's baseless accusations of widespread fraud following the oncoming shellacking that is heading MAGA's way in the November midterm elections.

The Supreme Court has been working overtime to find convenient pathways to enable Trump's unprecedented attack on American elections and democracy. And by turning the other way while Trump creates a flawed and false profile of every voter, they just found it.
State supreme courts are, without any doubt, now our very last line of defense against the impending fascist assault on free and fair elections.

You played by the rules.** **And now you're being asked to stretch your retirement dollars further and further while Washington fights over how much more taxpayers should provide.** But why should, you, an American taxpayer, be expected to shoulder migrants draining our public resources? Instead of supporting our families and saving our hard-earned money, Democrats are emphatic about suing Trump to stop him. | Letter from the Chair
---
| Friends,
From the day I became NEGOP Chairman, one mission has guided everything we do: unite this party for a fight we all knew was coming. Midterms are hard on the party holding Washington. History is not on our side unless we make it so.
We are as united as I have ever seen us -- not around personalities, but around a shared duty: defend Nebraska from the sharp left turn Democrats have taken these last two years.
We still have the Good Life. Not a perfect life. A good one.
Safe communities. Neighbors who show up. Extraordinary common sense. No boys in girls' sports. Meritocracy instead of DEI. Secure borders versus open borders. That is worth protecting and defending. It is also easy to take for granted. When life is good, complacency creeps in. Apathy looks like "someone else will handle it."
This year, that excuse is gone. Across the ballot, Democrat candidates have shown that what they say in Nebraska is not what they mean once the cameras are off. People who were sleepwalking through this election have woken up. Momentum is with us. Momentum dies if we ease off.
None of our work matters if you do not vote -- and if you do not bring your friends and family with you.
The NEGOP, our county parties, and Republican campaigns are already on the doors, on the phones, writing postcards, and sending texts. There is a job for every temperament and every schedule. You can call or text from anywhere in the state. For the first time, NE.GOP has a statewide candidate slate (see below) that you can sort by county. Find your races. Share them. Use them.
We are not doing this alone. Republicans and right-leaning groups are pulling the same direction: keep the radical left from gaining ground in Nebraska. TPUSA Action has been mailing voter-registration pieces -- I received one myself. Citizens for Free Enterprise is knocking doors here and in other states. PACs are funding campaigns and putting voter information in people's hands. Faith communities are awake and moving their members.
Thirty-nine days. November 3 is not far off. Make every one of those days count. Donate to a campaign. Vote. Take someone with you. Knock a door. Make a call. Send a text. Defend the Good Life.
Together we win!
In Liberty and in Truth,

| A Message From Senator Pete Ricketts...
I'm Proud to Fight for Rural Nebraska. Dan Osborn Mocks Rural Nebraska. Over the last month I've had the chance to travel across Nebraska and hear from the people I serve. Hardworking Nebraskans told me what matters most to them.
Every stop showed exactly why Nebraska is worth fighting to protect. In North Platte, Sustainable Beef processes 1,500 cattle a day. It contributes $1 billion to the local economy. We fought to make that producer-owned facility a reality. In Kearney, a new health education complex is training more doctors and nurses. We secured $60 million for that project. We have also brought jobs to Columbus, Blair, and communities across the state. It was great to see these investments paying off.
Back in Washington, we are delivering. I helped pass the historic tax cuts keeping more money in your pocket. I have fought to secure the border and enforce our immigration laws. I have stood up for Nebraska farmers and ranchers. We are expanding markets and increasing demand for homegrown biofuels.
The choice this November is clear. I love rural Nebraska. I have spent my career delivering for it. Dan Osborn sees it differently. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139953257/649055735/-569431239?refcode=260925-fake&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwOGFkODdiMy0wMGI5LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=iL26upBrLTJ3NlLFAIQsqhEz0dWqGiGPTdFmqcvrr7o=)

My office is already getting reports of it: mail about your voter registration or whether you can vote that doesn't come from any official source. Groups that send this kind of mail often use outdated or wrong information about voters. That's no accident. Confusion is the whole point.**I won't pretend we know yet who's behind every one of these mailers. But we know the playbook, and it's the same one we've watched all year.** **First,** Donald Trump tried to use an executive order to control who gets a ballot through the Postal Service. In a state that votes entirely by mail, that could have frozen our elections. Oregon fought back, and the Supreme Court shut him down 7–2. **Now** the attacks are coming quietly: out-of-state callers pushing false election information, and mail meant to make you doubt whether you're registered or whether your ballot counts.**It's always the same goal.** If Trump and his dark-money allies can't change the rules, they'll try to make you give up on the system before you ever vote. **Here's how to beat it. Real election mail carries the official logo, with the stars and stripes, the words "Official Election Mail," and "Authorized by the U.S. Postal Service." If you're unsure, check your registration at oregonvotes.gov or call your county clerk.** Oregonians trust vote-by-mail because it works, and I'm not going to let anyone scare people out of it. But fighting disinformation takes resources: getting accurate information to voters, answering every lie quickly, and standing up to Republicans who want to rig this system for themselves. **[Can you chip in $10 right now to my campaign so we can amplify this information and fight back against these election games?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139953258/649055736/-569431239?refcode=260925-fake&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwOGFkODdiMy0wMGI5LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=iL26upBrLTJ3NlLFAIQsqhEz0dWqGiGPTdFmqcvrr7o=)**

**Hey****,**
I have to be honest, we have less than a week until the last FEC deadline before early voting starts in Ohio, and I don’t want to sugarcoat how things look right now.
When Fairshake, a crypto-backed super PAC, announced it was spending $30 million on this campaign, we saw overwhelming support from everyday people who stand against the $238 million in Republican spending I’m now up against.
But since then, **our fundraising has hit a deep slump** , and in the next few days we may have to make budget cuts – while dark-money groups get to spend millions a day in Ohio. _Combined Republican groups are outspending us 7:1 every day right now._
We know that not everyone can chip in – and we don’t expect folks to donate to every email we send out, but with enough support we can get through the finish line and come out strong in November.
**[Will you please chip in $5 to my campaign today? This fundraising slump is coming at the worst possible time, and we have to close the gap between my campaign and the special interest groups spending in Ohio.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139953525/649056586/-1664069836?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=email_fr_gmailnd_jtk6188&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0MDg3ZDkyMy0wMWI5LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LLXTAvZ-OWB78d9U7ALLKBs3cXq_XORlsT85JSpkjzg=)**
| | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139953526/649056587/-1664069836?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=email_fr_gmailnd_jtk6188&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0MDg3ZDkyMy0wMWI5LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LLXTAvZ-OWB78d9U7ALLKBs3cXq_XORlsT85JSpkjzg=)
---
This race is in a dead heat, and Republicans know the spending they are pouring in will move the needle in their direction, and we can’t afford to let that happen. The latest ad blitz has brought this race into a statistical tie, and a poll released yesterday by Quantum Polling has us 47-47 against my opponent.
Every election expert has said the same thing – that this race is anyone’s game. We’re one of two races consistently ranked a “toss-up” by every major race rater. That’s not an accident.
We’re days away from the last reporting deadline before early voting starts in Ohio. If we show any signs of weakness, National Republicans will jump at the opportunity to keep spending hundreds of millions in Ohio. subject: Charlie saw something rare in JD Vance
body:
What this says about this moment in America | | | |
---
| | | Patriot,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Peter Willis,

Trump’s new $2.8 BILLION arms deal for Israel, including 40,000 MASSIVE

going to stop it.

New Gaza Complicity Accusations

The sale is already facing resistance in Congress thanks to widespread
public pressure. First a Democrat in the House announced a hold on the
sale — and then a key senator withheld her approval of the sale, citing
concerns about how the weapons would be used.

That’s progress. But a hold alone won’t stop this deal — we need to keep
up the pressure.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39799?source=email-20260925&t=1013&akid=11358%2E5885482%2EoYQ_E0 ]Take action: Tell Congress to pass a Joint Resolution of Disapproval
(JRD) to BLOCK Trump’s $2.8 billion bomb sale to Israel.

to Israel

Despite the "ceasefire", the reality is Israel continues to carry out
strikes in Gaza, killing on average one child each day.

But instead of scaling back our arms transfers, Trump’s latest arms
transfer would be one of the LARGEST in U.S. history, REWARDING the
Israeli government’s ongoing assault on Gaza and the West Bank.

Thanks to public pressure, more and more Democratic lawmakers are stepping
forward to oppose these sales. In April 2026, more than three dozen Senate
Democrats voted to block arms sales to Israel. Now we need to grow that
number even more to actually stop this deal.

Lawmakers need to know that people across the country are watching — and
that they cannot ignore the growing demand for the U.S. to stop enabling
genocide. When lawmakers step up, we have to have their backs. And when
others stay silent, we have to turn up the pressure.

That means flooding congressional offices with messages, amplifying the
lawmakers who are taking action, and making sure our representatives
understand that we expect them to use every tool available to stop this
sale.

And when the vote is finally scheduled, we’ll be there — ready to make our
voices heard in the critical hours and days before Congress decides.

name: The Turning Point USA Team
subject: Charlie saw something rare in JD Vance
body:
A story of faith lost, tested, and found again| | | |
---
| | | Patriot,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

Peter, a recent headline from the Decision Desk HQ says it all: **“Republicans look unlikely to gain much
— if anything — from redistricting”** The only reason that this is true is because YOU and this movement refused to back down and let Donald Trump get his way. For months now, the NDRC have been on the front lines of efforts that have blunted Republican attempts to rig the midterms in their favor. **Together, we’ve shut down gerrymanders in some states, passed countermeasures in others, and ensured that the will of the people will be heard this November.** Here’s the bad news: Today, anti-democracy forces are already laying the groundwork for the next chapter of this redistricting crisis. And it’s going to start _immediately_ following the midterms. We expect that Republicans in states like Georgia and Texas could go right back to work to pass new gerrymanders even if — _especially if_ — voters kick them out of office. **The NDRC has a strategy for continued resistance and mobilization against every attempt, present and future, that aims to unfairly rig our maps.** That includes our work building political power by electing Democracy Defenders and holding bad actors accountable at the polls — but it also must include being ready to fight back on the ground in the states where the next map manipulation happens. | | Hey Peter, **I was in New York City for Climate Week, meeting with leaders and advocates from around the globe to discuss how we can take**** _real_****action on climate change, and to bring what’s happening right now in Oregon into those conversations.** Climate change is not some distant threat. **Our farmers are living it right now.** I’ve heard directly from farmers who are committed to farming, but drought, wildfire smoke impacts, fuel and fertilizer costs, workforce challenges, and low market prices for their crops make it nearly impossible to break even. They are desperate for stability so they can raise their families, feed our communities, and keep Oregon agriculture alive. This year, on top of all of that, our pear growers here in District 3 are facing devastating losses of upwards of $60 million due to a destructive pest infestation. **If we want healthy food grown here in America, we need to build systems that support the people growing it.** That means addressing climate change, helping farmers adapt, and making sure relief reaches them when they need it. And we cannot talk about climate change without talking about the companies that have contributed to it and continued to profit while our communities pay the price. **Big Oil needs to pay its fair share.** That’s why I introduced **three bills** to hold oil and gas companies accountable, protect taxpayers, and support communities harmed by pollution. Climate change is already affecting Oregon. We need to stop talking about it as a future problem and start treating it like a present crisis. **[Can I count on you to donate $5, $10, or even $20 today as I work to provide real support and relief for our farmers and hold Big Oil accountable? clean_body: | | | = | | Hey Peter, I was in New York City for Climate Week, meeting with leaders and advocates from around the globe to discuss how we can take realaction on climate change, and to bring what’s happening right now in Oregon into those conversations. Climate change is not some distant threat. Our farmers are living it right now. I’ve heard directly from farmers who are committed to farming, but drought, wildfire smoke impacts, fuel and fertilizer costs, workforce challenges, and low market prices for their crops make it nearly impossible to break even. They are desperate for stability so they can raise their families, feed our communities, and keep Oregon agriculture alive. This year, on top of all of that, our pear growers here in District 3 are facing devastating losses of upwards of $60 million due to a destructive pest infestation. If we want healthy food grown here in America, we need to build systems that support the people growing it. That means addressing climate change, helping farmers adapt, and making sure relief reaches them when they need it. And we cannot talk about climate change without talking about the companies that have contributed to it and continued to profit while our communities pay the price. Big Oil needs to pay its fair share. That’s why I introduced three bills to hold oil and gas companies accountable, protect taxpayers, and support communities harmed by pollution. # Iran recycled June's deal. Now it's a 7-day clock
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the Strait of Hormuz can reopen in 7 days and nuclear talks **[can restart if the U.S. meets conditions](https://substack.com/redirect/c8811e16-2e06-4937-a7e0-634c2f6f589b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** already in **[June's collapsed memorandum.](https://substack.com/redirect/e304cc3c-c693-49b8-8227-fe79e0a95bec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f140229f-5d02-4037-8aa9-476c95fc35ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Islamabad terms get recycled:** Araghchi said the conditions match the Islamabad MOU Trump signed in June. That ceasefire collapsed in early July, and the administration has said it will not return to those terms.
* **Oil slips on talks:** Brent November[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/6655f045-52a2-4ad2-8ea0-60bbf78dc716?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[futures fell 1% to $105.56](https://substack.com/redirect/6655f045-52a2-4ad2-8ea0-60bbf78dc716?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and WTI[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/9f6d2c13-1821-4a8c-9856-53a58bcee52e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[fell 1.8% to $92.94.](https://substack.com/redirect/9f6d2c13-1821-4a8c-9856-53a58bcee52e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Vessel transits through Hormuz, normally about a fifth of global oil, fell to 9.
* **Houthis hit Saudi targets:** Houthis fired dozens of missiles and drones at Saudi targets Friday; authorities intercepted 6 ballistic missiles. Pezeshkian said the Houthis "are responsible for their own actions."
* **Senate rejects war pullout:** The Senate[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/b74917c8-6880-4a5e-80c3-423abc2646cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[voted 49-50 Thursday against a concurrent War Powers measure](https://substack.com/redirect/b74917c8-6880-4a5e-80c3-423abc2646cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** directing Trump to pull U.S. forces from Iran. Tillis, Collins, Murkowski, and Paul voted yes; Fetterman was the lone Democrat no.

For retirement savers 55 and up, that's not an abstract economic debate. It's the difference between a nest egg that keeps pace and one that quietly loses ground every year, even while the account balance looks "fine" on a statement.
Physical gold has held real value through currency devaluations, recessions, and political dysfunction for longer than any fiat currency has existed. And there's a mechanism most investors never hear about at a workplace benefits meeting: a Gold IRA can hold IRS-approved gold and silver, and in many cases, a portion of an existing IRA, 401(k), or TSP can move into one without triggering a current tax bill or penalty.
Gold Gate Capital has handled these rollovers since 2008. Qualified purchases may include up to $25,000 in free silver under current terms.
