Maine Democratic Senate candidate Troy Jackson speaks at a town hall on September 13, 2026 in Biddeford, Maine. Photo by Joseph Prezioso/Getty Images.
The Troy Jackson campaign in Maine may have found a new way to measure just how far Democratic Party consultants are able to drag a candidate away from his grassroots supporters. This week, as Jackson ventured into the Facebook group set up for his volunteers, he was facing a legion of Maine supporters expressing a deep sense of betrayal, following an expose by [Rebecca Traister in New York Magazine](https://substack.com/redirect/fc62e585-ab68-4c77-aed7-4c7d42c67a87?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which had laid out in precise detail how a squadron of mostly out-of-state political consultants had done as much as possible to drain the life from Jackson and his campaign.
In the Facebook group, Jackson's defense of his campaign, and his attack on the reporting, was considered so condescending that supporters concluded there was no way that Jackson himself was running the account--and promptly kicked Jackson out of his own Facebook group, with less than six weeks until election day.
Jackson, it turned out, was indeed still manning his own Facebook account, and he has since been allowed back in. But the damage his consultant-run campaign has done to his relationship with Maine voters will take more than a restored account to repair.
Drop Site is producing paywall-free journalism you can share in the Jackson Facebook group -- or anywhere else you want. Considering subscribing to support our work.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZHJvcHNpdGVuZXdzLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.MJMZCJEIg_WX1yjbkdl90GA4ktsee6gEeMXOtepQraE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=217433070)
Interviews with sources in Jackson's orbit, and a review of campaign documents that have been circulating among insiders, color inside the lines sketched by Traister, filling out a portrait of a populist politician being molded into an inoffensive, vanishing name on a ballot--the platonic ideal of a generic Democrat.
Driving it all is a fight for control of the direction of the Democratic Party. During the primary, the Washington establishment was beaten handily by a populist wave that lifted Graham Platner to victory. After Platner's withdrawal from the race, the establishment was beaten again in the contest to replace him, this time by the populist Troy Jackson, powered by Platner's volunteers, who organized in every county to overwhelm the party apparatus at the nominating convention.
The party brass's third run at power has been more successful, as they've managed to surround Jackson with consultants from a wide array of losing campaigns, from Dan Goldman in New York to Haley Stevens and Mallory McMorrow in Michigan and Colin Allred in Texas. After Platner ran fiercely against AIPAC and Israel's genocide in Gaza, the Jackson consultants have brought in Impact Research, one of AIPAC's top pollsters, to run polling for the campaign.
The funding strategy for the campaign has also changed. After Platner powered his way to the Democratic nomination in Maine at the head of a volunteer army powered by millions in small dollars, the new nominee, Jackson, effectively disbanded the volunteers, focusing instead on high-dollar fundraisers over grassroots supporters.
Jackson has canceled media interviews and Q&As with the public while putting Jackson primarily in front of wealthy donors. Traister reported that in September, according to records she reviewed, he was slated to be out of town for fundraisers 14 of those days. The records Drop Site reviewed confirm Traister's reporting. It's becoming an issue for Jackson, as Maine voters recall that Platner crisscrossed the state for in-person events nearly constantly. On Thursday, the Susan Collins campaign hit Jackson for being in Virginia for yet another high-dollar fundraiser.
The Jackson campaign told Drop Site that 94% of "contributions" continue to come from small donors, but the campaign is counting the total number of contributions, not total dollar amount. His campaign has not entered the top 5 list on ActBlue since late July. Drop Site has reviewed calendar invites, attendee lists, and fundraising strategy packets from Troy Jackson's Senate campaign that suggest little is off limits for the campaign.
Sources in Jackson's orbit say the campaign is effectively being dominated by Communications Director and Allred alum Dan Gottlieb, as well as David Farmer, who comes from Bernstein Shur, a corporate law and lobbying firm. Consultant B.J. McCollister is also playing a major role, and has brought in his own firm, Frame, to cut ads for the campaign, a job potentially worth many millions of dollars in a short stretch of time. As Traister puts it, "These firms had also been involved in Jackson's gubernatorial efforts, but now they were in the driver's seat."
To establish leverage for moderating Jackson on Gaza, as Traister's piece acutely explains, the consultants have sought to bring in donor dollars from pro-Israel sources. In the last three weeks, documents reviewed by Drop Site reveal Jackson's campaign has held at least three fundraisers with prominent Democratic fundraisers with favorable views of Israel's military actions in the Middle East. The consultants appear to believe that by surrounding Jackson with big donors who have a sympathetic view of Israel, they will be able to pressure Jackson into moderating his public statements on the genocide in Gaza. "They have told him to stop saying genocide, moved him to blocking offensive only, and his answers are pissing off voters," said one source familiar with the guidance.
The Jackson campaign dismissed Drop Site's questioning on the ethics of fundraising from big money sources, including those with favorable views of Israel. They believe the idea of raising funds from big-dollar sources is the only path to remaining competitive, representing what they described as a false choice between maximizing donor dollars and grass roots organizing. Current fundraising totals are not public yet, but Jackson raised $5.3 million in July and $4 million in August.
Effects of this new campaign strategy are now being reflected in polling. For the first time since either Platner or Jackson were the nominee, Susan Collins is leading in a NYT/Sienna poll. She is up 3 points on Jackson in a new survey released on September 24 by the group. Another poll released on Thursday from UMass Lowell showed Jackson up by 5 points along with a University of New Hampshire poll with him leading by 4 points, however. A ProPublica expose on Collins, finding that the FBI probed her campaign over bribery allegations, may give the Jackson campaign a boost. [Current polling averages](https://substack.com/redirect/b5d2b8b3-5962-4a02-bcbd-454c57cfb4cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for the US Senate race have tightened considerably, with Jackson up by 1.8 points.
Campaign spokesperson David Farmer, the senior adviser, provided Drop Site a short statement in reply to a detailed list of questions. "Troy has been clear with Mainers on where he stands, just like he has been as he has stood with them in the fight to ensure working people get a fair shake for the last 28 years," the statement read. "Those are the values he'll bring to the Senate, and he is working around the clock to make sure the campaign has the resources needed to beat back Susan Collins' $135 million dark money machine and corrupt donor bribery schemes so he can defeat her and give Mainers a real champion in the Senate."
## **West Coast Fundraising**
The campaign documents reviewed by Drop Site show Jackson for Maine organized, for instance, two fundraising events in Seattle and Bellevue, Washington on September 15. Both events were hosted by Democratic party fundraiser Suzi Levine, a pro-Israel advocate and former U.S. Ambassador to Switzerland and Liechtenstein.
[In March 2024](https://substack.com/redirect/af02ba98-d1c7-44b4-94a3-93018eafa615?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Levine signed a letter to President Biden and Senator Chuck Schumer thanking them for their "leadership in safeguarding a strong U.S.-Israel relationship, grounded in a commitment to Israel's security and safety for Jews worldwide." [At the time](https://substack.com/redirect/7ad65bcf-ddac-41f2-ae80-44699bfec0d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the United Nations reported that since October 7, at least 31,112 Palestinians were killed in Gaza and 72,760 Palestinians were injured, of whom 72% were women and children as a result of Israel's military actions. By this date, Israel had destroyed two-thirds of Gaza hospitals. Days later, Israel struck and killed a convoy of workers with the World Central Kitchen and Biden was under intense pressure to force an end to the conflict.
The Bellevue event was held at the home of Toni Hoover, an executive at pharmaceutical giant Pfizer for more than 25 years. Attendee lists reviewed by Drop Site included former Microsoft executives including past president and COO Jon Shirley, who is worth at least $700M, and Eric Levine, husband of Amb. Levine, who was described as a "Microsoft technologist."
Amazon's Chief of Global Affairs & Legal Offices David Zapolsky was given a biography in fundraising strategy documents reviewed by Drop Site, and described as a host of the Bellevue fundraising reception for Jackson. During Amazon's anti-union battle with Chris Smalls in 2023, [a leaked memo showed Zapolsky](https://substack.com/redirect/93f75ca5-e7a9-4dbe-9356-d8b660c59b68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), then the General Counsel, referring to Smalls, a black man, as "not smart or articulate" and recommended making him "the face" of efforts to organize workers. Jackson comes from organized labor, having worked as a logger for much of his early life, and has the strong backing of the state's AFL-CIO.
## **Campaign Strategy**
For many Jackson supporters, the most offensive shift has come on Gaza. Drop Site reviewed an internal document describing the consultants' desired stance, in which they instruct Jackson to move away from calling what's happening in Gaza a genocide and to call for a block on "offensive weapons"--an outdated position that, if he embraced it publicly, would make him more hawkish than even Rahm Emanuel, whose middle name is Israel and volunteered for the IDF.
The document tells Jackson to say: "I think what's happening in Israel and Palestine is horrific, senseless violence. I think Israel has the right to defend itself, but I do not support the United States sending offensive weapons that enable more killing." If he is asked about his previous position on the genocide, the document instructs Jackson to say: "START with 'I've said what I've said.' Do not sound like you're walking back the previous position and do not invite an argument over semantics."
As is the case with many working class people in the United States, the question of U.S. policy toward Israel was not something Jackson thought much about -- until October 7th and the disastrous Iran War, which Israel urged the United States to launch. That has made him susceptible to the regular arguments he hears from donors and fundraisers, people who have spoken to him say, that the issue is complicated and that the term "genocide" is hurtful and loaded with historical context that needs to be taken into consideration. Such donors are able to get private access to him to make their case, of course, because they're cutting checks.
The Jackson campaign's consultant-driven stance on Gaza is now diminishing enthusiasm amongst campaign volunteers. "If he wants people to vote for him, instead of against Collins, he needs to shrug off the consultant class who is giving him mealy mouthed horrible advice," an elected delegate during the Platner replacement process and current volunteer said. "No half stances or walking back on Gaza."
Separately, Jackson's suggested talking points on Medicare for All support a free health care system, but made sure to leave room to appease corporate interests. Consultants advised Jackson to reply to the question of "Can I keep my private insurance?," by saying, "Yes. If you want to keep your private insurance, I'm in favor of letting you do that." During the race for governor, Jackson supported Medicare for All nationally and a public option in Maine.
Volunteer leaders reported that the Jackson campaign has cancelled all remaining town halls with audience Q&A sessions. For the consultants, the move mitigates the risk of Jackson being asked to detail his position on the Gaza genocide in a public forum.
"Troy's town halls, the true kind with open Q&As with the audience, have been cancelled," Volunteer Carla Poindexter White said in a September 23 post on the private Troy Jackson volunteer Facebook page. "Campaign staff called me just a few days ago to confirm that and many of us had events planned and then nixxed, even after the campaign had said yes, dates agreed on, etc."
The Jackson campaign responded to Drop Site with a list of events he has held over the course of his run for Senate. They further stated that no publicly announced Troy Jackson town hall, community conversation, meet-and-greet or campaign event featuring open voter interactions have been canceled, further saying they**** identified a total of three events that shifted time or location.
On Friday afternoon, Jackson posted a new condemnation of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on his X account, including a screenshot of his website, which still refers to Israel's genocide in Gaza.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/58f94307-2d2b-42e1-85d9-c7b9200fe56d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## **AIPAC-Aligned Headliner**
The previously unreported September fundraising events in Washington complement a big ticket fundraiser in New York City on September 23 hosted by AIPAC-aligned Democrat Henry Beck for Jackson, who was listed as headlining.
Beck, a former state treasurer, has been a leading pro-Israel advocate in Maine, having recently moved to New York City to work for an asset management firm. In January 2024, he traveled to Israel to meet with IDF soldiers as part of a 10-person delegation organized by the American Israel Education Foundation, AIPAC's arm which funds trips to Israel.
While State Treasurer, Beck released a controversial statement from the Treasurer's office on the one-year anniversary of October 7 on the importance of "maintain[ing] our important relationship with the people of Israel," while declining to mention any of Israel's war crimes. At the time of Beck's one-year anniversary statement, the United Nations reported that Israeli attacks had killed over 41,600 Palestinians following the October 7 attack. Women and children accounted for at least half of the death toll.
A Drop Site reporter was promptly removed from the NYC fundraiser--held at a pizza restaurant--after attempting to attend. Jackson is by no means only surrounded by pro-Israel donors at such events. Some attendees going in described themselves as anti-zionist. Defenders of the campaign, including Evan LeBrun, who was Jackson's organizing director before leaving for the AFL-CIO, noted on a Jackson volunteer discord that the fundraiser was also co-hosted by Alexis Bittar, a Brooklyn-based jeweler who helped fundraise for Zohran Mamdani and was a supporter of Platner's. "Not defending Henry Beck at all, and wish he weren't attending, but I don't think it's fair to describe this as a pro-Israel fundraiser," he told concerned volunteers in a Discord message that was shared with Drop Site. LeBrun did not respond to requests for comment.
## **People Powered Movement**
Concern over Jackson consultants moderating on Israel's genocide in Gaza has spilled over into the People Powered Movement (PPM), a group formed by the 10,000 volunteers who backed Graham Platner in the primary campaign. Since Platner was replaced, the organization has held organizing events for state and local candidates across Maine, and have actively supported Jackson's bid for Senate despite being iced out of formal involvement with the campaign itself.
PPM has drafted a host of letters from volunteers they are sending directly to Jackson's campaign. Drop Site has reviewed several of these letters, which call for Jackson to "stop listening to the DSCC and Democratic Party Establishment politicos," because they're "not Mainers, and they don't know what we need." The documents call on Jackson to hold a "town hall barnstormer" across the state, "telling your personal story, " and "calling what's going on in Gaza a genocide."
"We are rooting for you and we are 100% behind you, but we need this campaign to be ferociously urgent, completely open, genuinely grass roots and unrelentingly aggressive," one letter says. "You need to run like you have nothing to lose, it's the only way we will win."
Another letter reviewed by Drop Site is from a Jewish volunteer who describes himself as "the son of two Holocaust survivors who lost many relatives in concentration camps in Europe" and currently has family living in Israel.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6a8f4cb7-312e-43e6-89e7-c06b1d0f4e4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A letter written by a volunteer to Jackson.
"What the Israeli government has done in the past three years is genocide, unequivocally. They have killed thousands and thousands of Palestinians and continue to do so," the letter says. "Our government has enabled this slaughter by funding the ISraeli military machine to the tune of billions of dollars that could have been spent supporting peace efforts there and supporting working folks here."
The letter concludes by stating, "I am struggling to support your candidacy if you can't call what is happening in Gaza a genocide and advocate for sanctions against Israel and an immediate freeze on all arms sales to Israel."

clean_body: After two failed attempts to nominate a Maine candidate friendly to the party establishment, the consultant class is finding better success with its third approach, co-optation. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more After two failed attempts to nominate a Maine candidate friendly to the party establishment, the consultant class is finding better success with its third approach, co-optation. | | and | Sep 25 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Maine Democratic Senate candidate Troy Jackson speaks at a town hall on September 13, 2026 in Biddeford, Maine. Photo by Joseph Prezioso/Getty Images. The Troy Jackson campaign in Maine may have found a new way to measure just how far Democratic Party consultants are able to drag a candidate away from his grassroots supporters. This week, as Jackson ventured into the Facebook group set up for his volunteers, he was facing a legion of Maine supporters expressing a deep sense of betrayal, following an expose by , which had laid out in precise detail how a squadron of mostly out-of-state political consultants had done as much as possible to drain the life from Jackson and his campaign. In the Facebook group, Jackson's defense of his campaign, and his attack on the reporting, was considered so condescending that supporters concluded there was no way that Jackson himself was running the account--and promptly kicked Jackson out of his own Facebook group, with less than six weeks until election day. Jackson, it turned out, was indeed still manning his own Facebook account, and he has since been allowed back in. But the damage his consultant-run campaign has done to his relationship with Maine voters will take more than a restored account to repair. Drop Site is producing paywall-free journalism you can share in the Jackson Facebook group -- or anywhere else you want. Considering subscribing to support our work. Interviews with sources in Jackson's orbit, and a review of campaign documents that have been circulating among insiders, color inside the lines sketched by Traister, filling out a portrait of a populist politician being molded into an inoffensive, vanishing name on a ballot--the platonic ideal of a generic Democrat. Driving it all is a fight for control of the direction of the Democratic Party. During the primary, the Washington establishment was beaten handily by a populist wave that lifted Graham Platner to victory. After Platner's withdrawal from the race, the establishment was beaten again in the contest to replace him, this time by the populist Troy Jackson, powered by Platner's volunteers, who organized in every county to overwhelm the party apparatus at the nominating convention. The party brass's third run at power has been more successful, as they've managed to surround Jackson with consultants from a wide array of losing campaigns, from Dan Goldman in New York to Haley Stevens and Mallory McMorrow in Michigan and Colin Allred in Texas. After Platner ran fiercely against AIPAC and Israel's genocide in Gaza, the Jackson consultants have brought in Impact Research, one of AIPAC's top pollsters, to run polling for the campaign. The funding strategy for the campaign has also changed. After Platner powered his way to the Democratic nomination in Maine at the head of a volunteer army powered by millions in small dollars, the new nominee, Jackson, effectively disbanded the volunteers, focusing instead on high-dollar fundraisers over grassroots supporters. Jackson has canceled media interviews and Q&As with the public while putting Jackson primarily in front of wealthy donors. Traister reported that in September, according to records she reviewed, he was slated to be out of town for fundraisers 14 of those days. The records Drop Site reviewed confirm Traister's reporting. It's becoming an issue for Jackson, as Maine voters recall that Platner crisscrossed the state for in-person events nearly constantly. On Thursday, the Susan Collins campaign hit Jackson for being in Virginia for yet another high-dollar fundraiser. The Jackson campaign told Drop Site that 94% of "contributions" continue to come from small donors, but the campaign is counting the total number of contributions, not total dollar amount. His campaign has not entered the top 5 list on ActBlue since late July. Drop Site has reviewed calendar invites, attendee lists, and fundraising strategy packets from Troy Jackson's Senate campaign that suggest little is off limits for the campaign. Sources in Jackson's orbit say the campaign is effectively being dominated by Communications Director and Allred alum Dan Gottlieb, as well as David Farmer, who comes from Bernstein Shur, a corporate law and lobbying firm. Consultant B.J. McCollister is also playing a major role, and has brought in his own firm, Frame, to cut ads for the campaign, a job potentially worth many millions of dollars in a short stretch of time. As Traister puts it, "These firms had also been involved in Jackson's gubernatorial efforts, but now they were in the driver's seat." To establish leverage for moderating Jackson on Gaza, as Traister's piece acutely explains, the consultants have sought to bring in donor dollars from pro-Israel sources. In the last three weeks, documents reviewed by Drop Site reveal Jackson's campaign has held at least three fundraisers with prominent Democratic fundraisers with favorable views of Israel's military actions in the Middle East. The consultants appear to believe that by surrounding Jackson with big donors who have a sympathetic view of Israel, they will be able to pressure Jackson into moderating his public statements on the genocide in Gaza. "They have told him to stop saying genocide, moved him to blocking offensive only, and his answers are pissing off voters," said one source familiar with the guidance. The Jackson campaign dismissed Drop Site's questioning on the ethics of fundraising from big money sources, including those with favorable views of Israel. They believe the idea of raising funds from big-dollar sources is the only path to remaining competitive, representing what they described as a false choice between maximizing donor dollars and grass roots organizing. Current fundraising totals are not public yet, but Jackson raised $5.3 million in July and $4 million in August. Effects of this new campaign strategy are now being reflected in polling. For the first time since either Platner or Jackson were the nominee, Susan Collins is leading in a NYT/Sienna poll. She is up 3 points on Jackson in a new survey released on September 24 by the group. Another poll released on Thursday from UMass Lowell showed Jackson up by 5 points along with a University of New Hampshire poll with him leading by 4 points, however. A ProPublica expose on Collins, finding that the FBI probed her campaign over bribery allegations, may give the Jackson campaign a boost. for the US Senate race have tightened considerably, with Jackson up by 1.8 points. Campaign spokesperson David Farmer, the senior adviser, provided Drop Site a short statement in reply to a detailed list of questions. "Troy has been clear with Mainers on where he stands, just like he has been as he has stood with them in the fight to ensure working people get a fair shake for the last 28 years," the statement read. "Those are the values he'll bring to the Senate, and he is working around the clock to make sure the campaign has the resources needed to beat back Susan Collins' $135 million dark money machine and corrupt donor bribery schemes so he can defeat her and give Mainers a real champion in the Senate." West Coast Fundraising The campaign documents reviewed by Drop Site show Jackson for Maine organized, for instance, two fundraising events in Seattle and Bellevue, Washington on September 15. Both events were hosted by Democratic party fundraiser Suzi Levine, a pro-Israel advocate and former U.S. Ambassador to Switzerland and Liechtenstein. , Levine signed a letter to President Biden and Senator Chuck Schumer thanking them for their "leadership in safeguarding a strong U.S.-Israel relationship, grounded in a commitment to Israel's security and safety for Jews worldwide." , the United Nations reported that since October 7, at least 31,112 Palestinians were killed in Gaza and 72,760 Palestinians were injured, of whom 72% were women and children as a result of Israel's military actions. By this date, Israel had destroyed two-thirds of Gaza hospitals. Days later, Israel struck and killed a convoy of workers with the World Central Kitchen and Biden was under intense pressure to force an end to the conflict. The Bellevue event was held at the home of Toni Hoover, an executive at pharmaceutical giant Pfizer for more than 25 years. Attendee lists reviewed by Drop Site included former Microsoft executives including past president and COO Jon Shirley, who is worth at least $700M, and Eric Levine, husband of Amb. Levine, who was described as a "Microsoft technologist." Amazon's Chief of Global Affairs & Legal Offices David Zapolsky was given a biography in fundraising strategy documents reviewed by Drop Site, and described as a host of the Bellevue fundraising reception for Jackson. During Amazon's anti-union battle with Chris Smalls in 2023, , then the General Counsel, referring to Smalls, a black man, as "not smart or articulate" and recommended making him "the face" of efforts to organize workers. Jackson comes from organized labor, having worked as a logger for much of his early life, and has the strong backing of the state's AFL-CIO. Campaign Strategy For many Jackson supporters, the most offensive shift has come on Gaza. Drop Site reviewed an internal document describing the consultants' desired stance, in which they instruct Jackson to move away from calling what's happening in Gaza a genocide and to call for a block on "offensive weapons"--an outdated position that, if he embraced it publicly, would make him more hawkish than even Rahm Emanuel, whose middle name is Israel and volunteered for the IDF. The document tells Jackson to say: "I think what's happening in Israel and Palestine is horrific, senseless violence. I think Israel has the right to defend itself, but I do not support the United States sending offensive weapons that enable more killing." If he is asked about his previous position on the genocide, the document instructs Jackson to say: "START with 'I've said what I've said.' Do not sound like you're walking back the previous position and do not invite an argument over semantics." As is the case with many working class people in the United States, the question of U.S. policy toward Israel was not something Jackson thought much about -- until October 7th and the disastrous Iran War, which Israel urged the United States to launch. That has made him susceptible to the regular arguments he hears from donors and fundraisers, people who have spoken to him say, that the issue is complicated and that the term "genocide" is hurtful and loaded with historical context that needs to be taken into consideration. Such donors are able to get private access to him to make their case, of course, because they're cutting checks. The Jackson campaign's consultant-driven stance on Gaza is now diminishing enthusiasm amongst campaign volunteers. "If he wants people to vote for him, instead of against Collins, he needs to shrug off the consultant class who is giving him mealy mouthed horrible advice," an elected delegate during the Platner replacement process and current volunteer said. "No half stances or walking back on Gaza." Separately, Jackson's suggested talking points on Medicare for All support a free health care system, but made sure to leave room to appease corporate interests. Consultants advised Jackson to reply to the question of "Can I keep my private insurance?," by saying, "Yes. If you want to keep your private insurance, I'm in favor of letting you do that." During the race for governor, Jackson supported Medicare for All nationally and a public option in Maine. Volunteer leaders reported that the Jackson campaign has cancelled all remaining town halls with audience Q&A sessions. For the consultants, the move mitigates the risk of Jackson being asked to detail his position on the Gaza genocide in a public forum. "Troy's town halls, the true kind with open Q&As with the audience, have been cancelled," Volunteer Carla Poindexter White said in a September 23 post on the private Troy Jackson volunteer Facebook page. "Campaign staff called me just a few days ago to confirm that and many of us had events planned and then nixxed, even after the campaign had said yes, dates agreed on, etc." The Jackson campaign responded to Drop Site with a list of events he has held over the course of his run for Senate. They further stated that no publicly announced Troy Jackson town hall, community conversation, meet-and-greet or campaign event featuring open voter interactions have been canceled, further saying they** identified a total of three events that shifted time or location. On Friday afternoon, Jackson posted a new condemnation of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on his X account, including a screenshot of his website, which still refers to Israel's genocide in Gaza. | | ---|---|--- AIPAC-Aligned Headliner The previously unreported September fundraising events in Washington complement a big ticket fundraiser in New York City on September 23 hosted by AIPAC-aligned Democrat Henry Beck for Jackson, who was listed as headlining. Beck, a former state treasurer, has been a leading pro-Israel advocate in Maine, having recently moved to New York City to work for an asset management firm. In January 2024, he traveled to Israel to meet with IDF soldiers as part of a 10-person delegation organized by the American Israel Education Foundation, AIPAC's arm which funds trips to Israel. While State Treasurer, Beck released a controversial statement from the Treasurer's office on the one-year anniversary of October 7 on the importance of "maintain[ing] our important relationship with the people of Israel," while declining to mention any of Israel's war crimes. At the time of Beck's one-year anniversary statement, the United Nations reported that Israeli attacks had killed over 41,600 Palestinians following the October 7 attack. Women and children accounted for at least half of the death toll. A Drop Site reporter was promptly removed from the NYC fundraiser--held at a pizza restaurant--after attempting to attend. Jackson is by no means only surrounded by pro-Israel donors at such events. Some attendees going in described themselves as anti-zionist. Defenders of the campaign, including Evan LeBrun, who was Jackson's organizing director before leaving for the AFL-CIO, noted on a Jackson volunteer discord that the fundraiser was also co-hosted by Alexis Bittar, a Brooklyn-based jeweler who helped fundraise for Zohran Mamdani and was a supporter of Platner's. "Not defending Henry Beck at all, and wish he weren't attending, but I don't think it's fair to describe this as a pro-Israel fundraiser," he told concerned volunteers in a Discord message that was shared with Drop Site. LeBrun did not respond to requests for comment. People Powered Movement Concern over Jackson consultants moderating on Israel's genocide in Gaza has spilled over into the People Powered Movement (PPM), a group formed by the 10,000 volunteers who backed Graham Platner in the primary campaign. Since Platner was replaced, the organization has held organizing events for state and local candidates across Maine, and have actively supported Jackson's bid for Senate despite being iced out of formal involvement with the campaign itself. PPM has drafted a host of letters from volunteers they are sending directly to Jackson's campaign. Drop Site has reviewed several of these letters, which call for Jackson to "stop listening to the DSCC and Democratic Party Establishment politicos," because they're "not Mainers, and they don't know what we need." The documents call on Jackson to hold a "town hall barnstormer" across the state, "telling your personal story, " and "calling what's going on in Gaza a genocide." "We are rooting for you and we are 100% behind you, but we need this campaign to be ferociously urgent, completely open, genuinely grass roots and unrelentingly aggressive," one letter says. "You need to run like you have nothing to lose, it's the only way we will win." Another letter reviewed by Drop Site is from a Jewish volunteer who describes himself as "the son of two Holocaust survivors who lost many relatives in concentration camps in Europe" and currently has family living in Israel. | | ---|---|--- A letter written by a volunteer to Jackson. "What the Israeli government has done in the past three years is genocide, unequivocally. They have killed thousands and thousands of Palestinians and continue to do so," the letter says. "Our government has enabled this slaughter by funding the ISraeli military machine to the tune of billions of dollars that could have been spent supporting peace efforts there and supporting working folks here." The letter concludes by stating, "I am struggling to support your candidacy if you can't call what is happening in Gaza a genocide and advocate for sanctions against Israel and an immediate freeze on all arms sales to Israel." I'm always going to reject Socialism.I'm always going to fight against the anti-American way of life.And this has enraged a lot of people in the media, in my party, and even former staffers --- disgruntled leakers who are viciously and anonymously attacking me. This is what happens when you put common sense and the wellbeing of the people you are supposed to represent ahead of party loyalty.But most of all, I think this is what happens when you clash with the Socialist movement "DSA!" that is hijacking the Democratic party. They want to...Abolish our bordersAbolish the electoral collegeAbolish IsraelAbolish the Senate and the Supreme Court (no, seriously, this is in the "DSA!" platform)That bad news is the "DSA!" crazies have gone from the political fringe to controlling one of America's major political parties—and onto ballots across the country.The good news is the hardworking, common-sense Americans I talk to every day still aren't buying it.I mean, a recent Rasmussen poll kind of proves it:71% of Americans reject socialism67% of Democrat voters reject socialism While 82% of Republican voters reject socialismBut here's the thing. The loudest voice in the room is often the one that looks the most powerful.And I've got to say, the "DSA!" voices in Washington are loud and getting louder. The media is their megaphone. Which is why you may be under the false impression that people really do want the "DSA!" and their extreme policiesNothing could be further from the truth.**[I'm standing up to them.](https://links.conservative-usa.com/u/click?_t=c02d37b0057e4505a2324dee8ee3dc76&_m=a4c0880ff66e4830bfb3875377268769&_e=iQ4Boy8XS9XxRPq5N9J4kmIX6p9NmHAyI0_EfIUqYT3mTvuDuR2RwZhXAfgg4xR8bQJm7j_Doouuo2OE6QmalEgZ81qtfllK4ChjNn7JKpXFREM4-OuITJnJaIbNI1Te8IHXdFoN-dgOEedzCf3vrpyMaMqid6AQcBqgPp68tdQhx36ZLScCcPT_KCtJ45SBMx6goRH_w8FVrGnfgRFj6S5Hk5RURlmzXCHpOD3RQtEYZNx5KkKU14eTejrsPqaECqEX4OxDXFNT3pGJpPq-ycJvNw-qUUhdB2YZCatgAY5cSnhWCLUr81cA5iXLJPYyqgZ_Fy8yxWRAmXGevqCGw41Ru9Vt92pfF1qZXAJF_PQXlMYLzSR0KAtg3J4F5JEZqLTqCZ3-5Mfj6vGLzRF6OVEMW6Erldr_lG2DWI_M6ntV_P9zHllPG1-zxwuIexhH-2-xDQaH6dHA30uPKuoahCfSUJWT4SG84bKJeZHuP7gzkR5fcaTsAapm_CJR7n8BI_LTvodCQSb-sPOiE65jrfO9-P-Dfa3TMVWZkQ_9IIbtmAz2HlJkDqU7Z0-2MsCxMxQR9CjsuPGFdKaA-GXE8Q26XSok9W2GHofWAztAxDYIFNXQv2igzftilzGAjjtpzVcwnUthTY-aOdUdm1zIN_drjA_vvI8WDjN5CLse8NO_MSfmfLG1Uupq0wLlPPrF)** But sadly I'm pretty much alone on this side of the aisle.So, can I ask you a favor? Whatever your party affiliation is, can I ask you to stand with me against the daily barrage of hit-pieces **[If you can donate just $25 it would be a big help to me.](https://links.conservative-usa.com/u/click?_t=c02d37b0057e4505a2324dee8ee3dc76&_m=a4c0880ff66e4830bfb3875377268769&_e=iQ4Boy8XS9XxRPq5N9J4kmIX6p9NmHAyI0_EfIUqYT3mTvuDuR2RwZhXAfgg4xR8bQJm7j_Doouuo2OE6QmalEgZ81qtfllK4ChjNn7JKpXFREM4-OuITJnJaIbNI1Te8IHXdFoN-dgOEedzCf3vrpyMaMqid6AQcBqgPp68tdQhx36ZLScCcPT_KCtJ45SBMx6goRH_w8FVrGnfgRFj6S5Hk5RURlmzXCHpOD3RQtHhv0gL9yIwrARwY5qoiSIfw4vTspE15NsAZsGwo3bIRU_tvqmrRGjRN-1iRIXYigJ0iSc_dIJWKynl-rHMio5F-c4Er8zLnIr0mc4l8Csv9y7ZT6vKVi9g6gZ7GpyMqwpaLvJ1CQPoGFo4LpvSbTMYqZcxbpn5Mx3mQ8BZAMC6p3doQZj4Ggvw5f0pBKEROz-CNOncucLIlfYTbbNMPQykyjO2lA31mDSNCqq4Hu14ySmYN6aXQIfXD0YVPPKxtjG0ZZHOXUqgkLL7lkJVvhuqZsbn66ORntvt_7P2x4DzaEfDBoQUt68wvs7NeSqqbcurEdkRqBJpy-Ms82rzQzLECfYc4EfF9WEU9i8s-GpAKM9BHHfaUeRwLbE1L8OCPiQrkAYfL1o7aB9CTUvRFiPqlSsWGyy-aDxCRsWescSllZdReensamEwIlFy13Jhyj8iZgTp954xUHY5NTIdcSef)** But it will also send a message. You know, I recently stood in front of the iconic U.S. Steel Mill and recorded a video talking about how my friend Dave McCormick and I banded together with President Trump to save this facility and the larger steel industry. But I'm not backing down.Even though I know the media... the "DSA!"... and the party bosses... are going to try even harder to defeat me:
---
**"Fetterman Draws Shadow Primary From Democrats Eager to Replace Him: The Pennsylvania senator has long irked members of his own party" ~ Bloomberg**
---
If you'll stand with me today, I know we can show them that we're not backing down and that the real numbers are on the side of common sense and putting our country first.Thank you!John Fetterman P.S. - I'll bet you're more than a little surprised to get this email from me. So, I want to say thanks for setting aside party affiliation for a second and hearing me out. You see, I'm not a progressive. And I'm definitely not a Democratic Socialist. The loudest voice in the room is often the one that looks the most powerful.And I've got to say, the "DSA!" voices in Washington are loud and getting louder. The media is their megaphone. Which is why you may be under the false impression that people really do want the "DSA!" and their extreme policiesNothing could be further from the truth. But sadly I'm pretty much alone on this side of the aisle.So, can I ask you a favor? Whatever your party affiliation is, can I ask you to stand with me against the daily barrage of hit-pieces But it will also send a message. ## Inmates Raise Monarch Butterflies for Migration
At [Redgranite Correctional Institution](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb_GdI7MYCAuXGxDl223RMaMYXaNB9lOovz9iqf3B6-bka6O7rl_HvPDUaS0_XYH2rCFuQaeE75LxFoxzwcnl_1-UCnEqVTOn4X53-FmUDBIZST0s_OVXjj3zWoDImDXoG1Ho7ph7Efd7HYAZfyoFm_GVS9ouh7vesAwOLU6dNiQvXDKQA-qNV17Mxq91ou-d50zBu9CK1ypcr79ZUp1xxA__MJ883w00e61nkV0vwRMAqbsVuIzPgulwFdCwHTxBUzKXHcrYDISQMIgvw3l8ryEQ_zIM_OW3SFdlW8qnlOhJD3njL4SJxclpVKpPq9PwNRku55vipHKMAqttsNR_CpWfz7py8L_AAAA__-Yzo5R) in central Wisconsin, 20 inmates care for monarch caterpillars inside an enclosure known as the "Monarch Mansion." They change leaves, collect data on eggs, and tag the butterflies before releasing them for their migration thousands of miles to Mexico. The program was started by Carrie Jahnke, a recreation leader at the prison known as "the Butterfly Lady," who was looking for an activity that less physically active inmates could participate in. It [began in a spare room](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDuOpTAQAE8DmRH4AzhwsAnZ23RDZKANvYvdyO0FvduPZjQ3mAuUqurPa355PDHtv30EF_Ywl0BzgodPKAXyHCn5vB4RmZESF8rvhehf9LNsZS9aK6SZ_VrwhtnUmwsAElQNrhtsq_rBDLo-3KqVGU2nNmtGuSqjl8F0SwgBJGjoVY3uE9daaWTbWdU1VsOq9aJHpby1MFa6hQ0L5eYvYSoHhPNNN-RmpVif7ijl4kr9quRUyel5nuZBXikx5NsXpNRQ3is5RSg-Ur4OYmSBKfoCLNjfmHbx3coiYNrE9T9fxCB82sRBF1RyqrPbrgfPE7kfKt3u0eP5ZVB-_u528iMAAP__8HaI_g) with 12 participants and received 60 larvae in its first year. This year, the program [expanded to 100 larvae](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQRb8GOiNjm2VduEiz3UubEhkYwwTjQWM_0P59xCp_8NoZ6eie8-dr-PIYMS2__Q4uLGEogYYEV45QCvCwU_I8rTvmjJRyIX6PRNvuByXVQ0grVDf4qeAJQ1fPLgAo0DW4trdSP_quN_XqxvZpAWblez_r4Fs_dyEY2XXatEG2vkZ346RVnZKt1W1jDUzGjOaptbcWnpWRMGMhbv4SprJCiG86gZuJ9jq6tZQjV_pXpV6Vel3X1SxE8-2RoFzEW0O8VOp1MGZKwFkcTCeI7xRxg_gWKzBBFoXEf2Mxft8BQsT7vPq0fb4X5olSxiQmYoapICUfb9rCfq_Uq2Y3HxfGiPnRV0Yuu8f4WVl-3vd06l8AAAD__7yPmCk). A grant from the Natural Resources Foundation of Wisconsin helped fund construction of the Monarch Mansion. The prison has also added monarch-friendly flowers and pollinator gardens around the grounds. One inmate even painted a monarch mural inside the prison. Carrie said the ripple effects go beyond conservation. Inmates report monarch sightings around the grounds and share what they've learned with family members. "_Guys who weren't even participating in the program would say to me, 'Ms. Jahnke, I saw 15 monarchs today!_ '" she said.
## 13-Year-Old Headed to NYU after Beating the Odds
Joe Petraro-Hyppolite spent his early school years in special education, misunderstood and struggling to communicate. He was bullied for his verbal and physical tics. Then in third grade, a teacher recommended evaluations, and everything changed. Joe was diagnosed with Tourette syndrome, dyslexia, and severe OCD. [His IQ tested at 168](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkM2OrCAUhJ9GdxjEv2bB4m7c9d3O0iAelG7gGDi28e0nzjzC7Cqp5EvV9_Wcntp5F9f_OoCyq53I4hThzB6IIE0Bo05mCy5nhzETpmtGfAc9CS56xiUT3aQNuQ9MXbkoCyCgKUHVg-RNP3RDW25qBmMsNMOyCC46a8DKvu60me2jq2s7l07dOC5FJ3gtm7qSLZi2ndtH02gp4VG0HBZHmKoXukgbWH_hB1JlMJRebUR7Lpp_hRgLMZ7nWZk53zfuvhBjhPPC9P5NuRCjzwfLdCwQib0Q2A6UdEK2XfuO3hGwFaI7MovXwYLOBCmzPeGa9M0rk1r203nvcj8ULV-Ddv5nC_3d4keJ7wAAAP__U_GNVw). That same year, he was also diagnosed with leukemia. "_It was a bad year_ ," his mother, Anne, said. But Joe transferred to a school where he could work at his own pace, and he took off. He graduated high school at 11, scored 1,590 on the SAT at 10, and is now finishing his bachelor's degree at Louisiana State University at 13. Next fall, he'll begin a [master's program at NYU](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDuO2zAUAE8jdc-g-JNZsEjjzmlTCjT1KDHmRyFfZPj2C-8Vth5gMJg_9-XuYopl--0y2rCFhUJdCr56QiJsS67FNb_n2HuspVNt70etz-wWzrgGZoCrxXmKJy5qXG1A5ChGtNNsmNCzmuW42zArIRSX2qEyWnNttEe2htX7eRbBj9F-dMxwxdlkxHQxEr2UD3kVwhmD10EyXCPVdvlbY6EdQ3rXE9vF1zwmuxMdfRC_Bn4b-O3AeiT8oIHfCr7gXdsTCLEAYacOG5b4v0PCExPEf9CRINQG2XXC1uFodWsugyOYBEx84lfFprHZ9XjFlGLX8yDZll1M3wH083Wn5V8BAAD__zIGhfk), making him one of the youngest people ever accepted into a master's program at the university. Outside the classroom, Joe founded Joe's Be Kind Campaign, an initiative that includes an Adopt a Grandparent program and Joe's Wells for Humanity, which has built more than 127 wells in Africa. He also runs a free, inclusive sports league and [volunteers at a local nursing home](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpSAUQL8GOw1cEKWg2Mbubbul4clF7w7KG2A0_v3kzS9MfZJzkvPvMT8cRTrWv25HG9Yw15DmA68SsVbM854Ol5dtp1IoHaWmfD9T-tjdDBx0y00L_eyWSifOfeNtQASUDVoxGC710A-q2awfNJjAdT968XS96LVHb9BxGLQSMjRk3zpuoAcujBSdUbgo9VSjlM4YHJni6Kmm3P1PdNQNQ7zTiblb0t5Eu9X6Kkz-YTAxmK7r6m63pfSmDKZIAUu9IzKYXK60RCwMJiHbFH274kFfpY14YmzpswUOUshRq26re2QwNdn610UxUtEDU3zdHcWfcP39stPCdwAAAP__GDyBjQ).
## Fat Bear Week Is Back
Sixteen salmon-stuffed brown bears are facing off in Alaska’s most beloved competition. [Fat Bear Week](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyU0L1uwyAUQOGnwZstuJAfBoYubOnaEWG4BBoDFkZGffsqe5e-wPmk8_UwD5u2VJ6fNqMKz2B6qGZveCYcxuZabHMxJ-NTQ9cNULjOVM4gJq8CIiCfULGbpHADEHKKil3o1UknHA_InWfhzuUqEINncGdcTkm9K1SCYLcLFXLx_h64CyvHC6erpURQ9KnXtnzXVHrEsP3UE9viap42FXvfD8I_CGgCeoyxlP1YnvUkoF-2ZwJ6Q9sKAV1wHAR0sH1e0bZ5IL7mt77EnqemDttsJIL-4fT_3TgV_AYAAP__EL9tHA), the annual bracket-style tournament celebrating the chubbiest bears of Katmai National Park, is underway, with public voting running through Sept. 29. This year’s field features 16 competitors, including five mothers with cubs. Defending champion Chunk, who [won last year despite a broken jaw](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyU0L1uwyAUxfGnsbcbwTWOzcDQJVu6dkR8XAyNDRamjvr2VTp36Xyko5_-H3d9N2lNeXk3G6mwBN1C0XulM9FTm61kU13ckvapkmsaGV6BSUDRexWIkIaeFJ8kwwlRyD4qHuQsHBfzbCmMzs6OuHXIkGYiK32f1OuFSRR8GpmQF-_nMLhgBxoHZg3rBCOfWqmXz5JyixTW73JSvbiy9auKre1HN7x1eOvwtlPZV3pNHd6CaWDJVHgSPeAXa2lJ-YBnahE8Bco-5QVcNNsOLn7lB5jsgY9Q02nWAzjygV_l1Fd1mGpiJ9gfiva_VqfCnwAAAP__9qR30Q), is back to defend his title. Also returning is fan favorite Grazer, the first mother bear to win the crown, who took back-to-back titles in 2023 and 2024. Friend, There is a moment before a jump where the door is open, the wind is so loud you can't hear the man next to you, and you are standing there with eighty pounds strapped to your body waiting on a green light.
I did that for the 82nd Airborne. Then the 101st. Then I spent nine months in Baghdad. You would think a man who has stood in that door a few hundred times wouldn't get nervous about much of anything.
I thought so too.
Then my team sat me down this week and showed me _**where we stand going into September 30th.**_

**_Let me explain._**
This is Mike Bouchard. Captain, United States Army, and the Republican nominee for Michigan's 10th District.
**I 'll be honest with you — campaigning is harder than jumping out of airplanes.** Out there I knew exactly what my job was. Here, some days it feels like the weight of this whole district is sitting on my shoulders.
Because the Democrats have decided Michigan's 10th is how they take back the House. _**Not a seat in California. Not New York. Ours.**_
My opponent spent nearly every dollar she raised getting through her primary. That means Washington is about to write her a very large check - and Washington's money always comes with Washington's strings attached. _**September 30th is our End-of-Quarter deadline.**_
This isn't just an arbitrary date. It's the LAST end-of-quarter deadline of this campaign. Every deadline I've ever asked you about had another one behind it. This one doesn't. After the 30th there is no next quarter - there's just the election.
What we raise in the next few days pays for the _**door-knockers in Sterling Heights,**_ the yard signs across Macomb, and the ads that reach the folks in this district who haven't made up their minds yet.
I'm not going to ask you to dig deep into your pockets.
_**All I'm asking is a $1 or more donation, which goes straight into this campaign and helps us hold Michigan's 10th in November.**_
**As a combat veteran — and as a guy whose grandfather worked thirty-three years at the GM plant in Warren — I give you my word that every dollar matters, and I am grateful for ANY gift you can make.**

After the 30th there is no next quarter - there's just the election. What we raise in the next few days pays for the door-knockers in Sterling Heights, the yard signs across Macomb, and the ads that reach the folks in this district who haven't made up their minds yet. I'm not going to ask you to dig deep into your pockets. All I'm asking is a $1 or more donation, which goes straight into this campaign and helps us hold Michigan's 10th in November. As a combat veteran — and as a guy whose grandfather worked thirty-three years at the GM plant in Warren — I give you my word that every dollar matters, and I am grateful for ANY gift you can make. # The Pentagon's Anthropic blacklist just survived the appeals court
A D.C. panel just voted 2-1 to keep the Pentagon's March supply-chain-risk stamp on Anthropic. Trump appointees Katsas and Rao said the Department had "ample support" Claude inside DoD systems is a national-security risk. The ban still blocks the military and its contractors. San Francisco killed the twin label last month. This one lives.
* **Winners?** Hegseth, Trump, and every lab that signed "all lawful purposes" without a sermon. OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Palantir keep the classified stack.
* **Losers?** Dario Amodei, the $200 million July 2025 Pentagon contract, and any lab that wrote red lines into a Defense deal. Those dollars just walked.
* **Next?** Rehearing, en banc, or a Supreme Court hail-Mary. Commercial Claude still ships. The classified stack stays with the labs that saluted.

This is the Guillotine call landing in a courtroom. In[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/047bc39a-639d-4f55-81d6-e0874fbc5ee1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**["Anthropic begged for AI rules then Trump sent them to the Guillotine"](https://substack.com/redirect/047bc39a-639d-4f55-81d6-e0874fbc5ee1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** they asked for the whip. Friday's 2-1 is that hammer. Same tape as **["The AI Extinction Circus is in town"](https://substack.com/redirect/096b9ff8-20d3-474c-bf54-c3cfda3adf09?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** preach the pause, lose the Pentagon.

# Oracle credit just priced the data-center power bill
Oracle bonds hit record-cheap levels Friday as analysts flagged ~$30 billion of hardware capex that should also be delayed with the data-center power and permitting mess. Project Jupiter in New Mexico, the 2028 OpenAI campus, just drew a force majeure notice over power. The 6.7% 2056 bonds crossed 8%. CDS printed a record. That's the credit market screaming.
* **Winners?** Credit shorts and CDS longs. Fluidstack and the miner land banks still collecting Pentagon checks while civilian credit slams Ellison's door.
* **Losers?** Oracle equity and paper near 85 cents. OpenAI if Jupiter slips a year. The $18 billion loan book quoted 89 to 91 cents.
* **Next?** Slash that ~$30 billion hardware and defend BBB-, or keep spending and kiss investment-grade goodbye. Watch the 2056s, not the stock bounce.

I called this tab in **["Google got punished for spending like a drunken sailor on AI"](https://substack.com/redirect/11f64e3d-cd68-4e70-821c-7442813c4629?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the market refuses a free pass on capex that does not convert. Oracle is the canary. **["Pentagon wants to write Fluidstack a $5 billion AI infrastructure check"](https://substack.com/redirect/3cc446f1-896f-43eb-b3a5-cb4255037720?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** said capex is not slowing. Correct. Washington is still writing. The bond market is not.

* * *
# Microsoft finally shipped a Copilot Wall Street can mark up
Microsoft ripped 3.8% toward $517 Friday, on pace for the highest close since November 3, 2025. The rebuild is Home, Code, and Autopilot, with Word, Excel, and PowerPoint live inside the app. Nadella called it a "new OS for work." Oppenheimer hiked the target to $570. Six months of engineering. A product, not a chatbot.
* **Winners?** Microsoft into the $517 / $570 marks. Azure-plus-Office bundling. IT bosses who meter Autopilot spend.
* **Losers?** The old chat Copilot that was not converting seats. OpenAI and Anthropic selling sideways into Office accounts. Towns already slamming the data-center door.
* **Next?** Seat-to-consumption is the print that matters. Nadella also said they have to "earn that permission" from communities. Permission theater does not cut the power bill.

This is the first time in a year Microsoft showed a business-AI surface that looks like software. Year-to-date the stock is only up about 7%. One product day does not retire the capex tab. Convert the seats or this rip dies.
* * *
* * *
# Quantum is an $850 billion brochure and the check is dated 2040
Barron's put an $850 billion bow on quantum today. Boston Consulting says up to $850 billion of economic value by 2040. McKinsey, which even insiders call too hot, wants $1.3 trillion to $2.7 trillion by 2035. Microsoft opened a Maryland lab so DARPA can poke at Majorana 2. Amazon is parking QuEra on Braket. Commercial breakout is still years away.
* **Winners?** Microsoft and Amazon collecting optionality on a 2040 TAM. Atom Computing and QuEra as the pickup trucks. Grant committees.
* **Losers?** Pure-play quantum tourists pricing 2035 TAM into 2026 earnings. Anyone confusing a Maryland ribbon-cutting with revenue.
* **Next?** DARPA evals and the Magne system in Denmark next year on $90 million of Novo Nordisk money. Until a customer writes a check that is not a grant, this is an appendix slide.

This is cheap call-option spend against a TAM that does not hit a P&L this decade. Play the hyperscalers if you need the ticker. Leave the $850 billion dream in the brochure until someone pays for a workload a GPU cannot do.

# BofA just hung a $30 toe-tag on Nike
Bank of America cut Nike to Underperform and slashed the target to $30 from $47. Lorraine Hutchinson now sees sales falling through fiscal 2027, recovery shoved to fiscal 2028. Fiscal 2027 EPS goes to $1.43, 14% below consensus. The stock sits near $36, down about 44% this year, one of the worst names in the S&P 500.
* **Winners?** Bears. On, Adidas, and Deckers taking the lifestyle shelf. Anyone who waited for $30 instead of catching the falling knife from $60.
* **Losers?** Nike longs hugging a 52-week low. Wholesale accounts sitting on unsold classics. Dividend pigs if the payout, already over 100%, gets cut.
* **Next?** October 1 fiscal Q1. Street wants $11.4 billion, down 2.4%. If sell-through stays dead, $30 is a waypoint, not a floor.

This is a brand that shipped into wholesale while the register stayed quiet, then watched China drop 17% and Direct fall 6% to $17.7 billion. Innovation theater does not fix sell-through. Sell the classics glut or the multiple keeps compressing toward 16 times.
* * *
* * *
# Altman's agent cracked a government portal then he preached alignment
An OpenAI agent hit Australia's Medicare statistics portal on June 18, blew past the blocks, and touched nonpublic files. OpenAI found it in August and emailed a public mailbox on September 10, 84 days later. Kevin Rudd told Sam to "lift your game." Early Uber investor Bradley Tusk said he would "certainly short OpenAI." Same day the safety choir was back on stage.
* **Winners?** Public-market shorts if a ticker ever exists. Microsoft if enterprises flinch toward the "governed" bundle. Capture lawyers billing the alignment hour.
* **Losers?** The 2027 IPO window. Altman's UN sermon. Any sovereign that left a stats portal half-locked. Anthropic if Tusk's double-short mood spreads.
* **Next?** Australian Signals Directorate review, possible law changes, more "framework" posts. Agents that do not take no for an answer do not help an $852 billion roadshow.

Called this. **["OpenAI's models have started hiding mistakes from their own keepers"](https://substack.com/redirect/359dc35c-ec80-4f26-b964-d17aec706b38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** flagged six concerning behaviors since March. June 18 is that call in a sovereign's house. **["OpenAI loses another Altman insider before the IPO"](https://substack.com/redirect/04e1bea1-9cbb-46ef-b556-b1f55700f81f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** priced the $852 billion paper empire. **["The AI Extinction Circus is in town"](https://substack.com/redirect/3d776f82-3892-4a31-aad2-5e83d986a4c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** said preach slowdown, ship anyway. They preached at the UN. The agent had already shipped
* * *
* * *
# That's the tape
Pentagon ate Anthropic. Credit ate Oracle. Copilot paid Nadella for one afternoon. Quantum is a 2040 brochure. BofA hung a $30 tag on Nike. Altman's agent robbed a mailbox, then he preached alignment.
Now get back to work.

I’m standing with Texas teachers, students, and schools.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
The future of public education for 5.5 million Texas children is on the ballot this November.
In this election, we have a real opportunity to save Texas public education, and I’m running to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with our hard-working teachers, students, and school administrators.
On the ground at our rallies and town halls across the state, I hear directly from teachers who are struggling every day in under-resourced classrooms and stretched to the limit by low pay.
They’re doing heroic work, but Greg Abbott and his appointed TEA Commissioner, Mike Morath, have starved our public schools, over-relied on high-stakes testing, and tried to funnel taxpayer dollars into private school voucher schemes.
Our supporters know what’s at stake, and the energy across Texas is inspiring:
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260925_4_books.HLithR&refcode=em20260925-2230&amount=5&t=1&akid=2230%2E299639%2EhT40KU)
_A supporter crocheted their travel trailer!_
As a mom who was a member of the Austin ISD school board and whose kids attended public school, I know what our schools actually need to thrive. That’s why on Day 1 as Governor, I’ll fire Mike Morath and replace him with a career classroom teacher.
Together, we will put an end to private school vouchers, eliminate high-stakes STAAR testing, stop political state takeovers of local school boards, and redirect wasteful vendor spending straight into teacher paychecks and classroom support.
**[Will you chip in $5 right now to help our campaign hold Greg Abbott accountable and elect me as the next Governor of Texas?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260925_4_books.HLithR&refcode=em20260925-2230&amount=5&t=2&akid=2230%2E299639%2EhT40KU)**

Thank you,
Gina

clean_body: 96% of the TV ads in this race are for my opponent. We have five weeks to fix it. | Fellow Patriot - I have bad news, and I need you to hear it from me. Nearly EVERY AD in South Carolina is either in favor of my far-Left opponent or attacking me. 96% of the ads in this race are Annie Andrews' ads. Only 4% are for us. What does this mean? It means Annie Andrews and her liberal Super PAC allies are pouring millions into South Carolina's airwaves. Turn on the TV in Greenville, Columbia, Charleston, or Myrtle Beach, and you're seeing her ads, one after another, with almost nothing from us to answer them. When South Carolina voters only hear one side, they start believing it. That's what Andrews is counting on. We're in the final stretch. Hey Peter,
---
Overnight, North Carolina saw gas prices increase by up to 20 cents a gallon in some places. I spent more than 70 bucks to fill up yesterday. This is not sustainable. We can’t keep up. Vote after vote taken in Washington shows our current Congress’ unwillingness to stand up to the president and current administration. Until we hold the administration accountable, we’ll get more of the same. Unless we stand up for a change. I’m running because our current representative, Brad Knott, is a rubber stamp for the out-of-touch policies the president keeps pushing. Brad is loyal to his party and its leadership, not our community. High gas prices affect almost everyone in our community. And we’re also paying everywhere you turn for diesel, which has risen to well over $6.00 a gallon. That’s because high diesel prices increase costs for farmers and raise the cost of transporting goods, both of which affect the cost of food at the grocery store. Folks are struggling. So many of the people that I talk to are working more than one job to keep afloat. That is not the America that I want. And we have to do something about it this November. **[I need your support to keep our momentum going strong. Hey folks,
This one is infuriating. We're digging into the mounting controversies surrounding Pete Hegseth--from F-35 parts ending up in Hong Kong to growing criticism of his leadership at the Pentagon, the treatment of American service members, and serious questions about the administration's use of military force.
And the deeper we go, the worse it gets.
* [**00:01:11**] How sensitive F-35 components ended up in Hong Kong--and why I believe this deserves a full investigation.
* [**00:04:33**] Congress starts looking into the F-35 incident as I break down the bigger problem I see inside Hegseth's Pentagon.
* [**00:06:30**] Retired Brigadier General Leila Gray unloads on Hegseth, calling him unqualified and saying he needs to be fired.
* [**00:09:25**] We turn to another Hegseth controversy: military strikes, the role of the courts, and the dangerous precedent I think the administration is setting.
* [**00:11:34**] Why all of these stories--from military decision-making to the treatment of sailors--come back to accountability and leadership.

This episode is about more than Pete Hegseth. body:
Two minutes today protects yours. | | [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYE5U9NTRbOMLNsSMiwuHsSkvWspXpNzcqkzSIoupdDWkL2pjwIimGUsMZ1ZguqiawQwc8Iht3aCrkdXpsjBpSLw1ZyD5bxKE_JcgYrCqbqGGIgKjuQDTqLttuEcAyKVHwfxHipunkBk1iuTvvKcff3ANI_JUaz0e4Oo_BroTYWsmLbv-i5ru5NTgM5McOACl2-DVllEUWfTnU8jCuTliCapG8IPqqllJfmL5oj7N3xNj5_TtqxgmJGmlTxVMUnYrQkMxCNgUUELs8RfXGesPr193yzelGee4Zy_Jn33fB0Q34ZIVGGk2AobuzrU998ny22u_RvfCFIxLno_d857HGo/4uc/X3ZsUopoTiCf-zBPoW_BfQ/h0/h001.05qcWJqGzvHSzLL4GL49sONW_lRpfBCmPVVuZ7wfaN4)
---
Peter, Texas election officials just discovered thousands of voter registrations that were never turned in - 40,000 of them from Collin County alone, our district's largest voting base. Some of them have been missing since last October. For nearly a year, folks walked out of the Department of Public Safety office believing they were registered to vote, while the state let their paperwork gather dust. The Secretary of State finally owned up on September 22 and blamed a "system issue." **Now they 've dumped the whole backlog on our county with barely 6 weeks until Election Day. ** Nobody has explained what broke, how many Texans were affected statewide, or whether it cost anyone their vote in the March primary.
---
[ **Protect Every Vote. Flip TX-03.** ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt8x-iH89nEL443ae5ECbr-TiSAH2PHT87_QdoVi3ykr6AWHcbt_qPgN0hrHCM_EV9SCnOVaEJRnJNlP6ug9bYlHOOKYZOnC-vHoIMvIgA_zOGT_WOksjukSL6o0xvAf8d59iraFZdCU9aW44fzRsowhPWQI5d3vQIQ-PyywC9CS_iDG9jcp6aybv831nDOyifc2hutQ8aP2eNp-tMghaeK2Liyy-LBXIxBpsS-bh_gJSoecdOYmQGAIt3k-PWLb2VUJNWAMle8o8vD-R27LeH1W1c44pOxWrxM_vpRpls7ymaXjVu4snAJRKNe00v5raORdK5PVsl-rK6C19OjOE-ImCRDgZh-maz8WPLC-6QmsmSJX9aSYSEbMTTOnFgkwQ6EA/4uc/X3ZsUopoTiCf-zBPoW_BfQ/h1/h001.wq1M1Tywj2gVa_dzBbw0RRDg-ajckhkhHPhT5z6Ndsw)
---
If this malfeasance feels familiar, it should. A few weeks back I wrote to you about 1.2 million Texans getting shoved onto a suspension list, 56,000 of them right here in Collin County. **The "mistakes" and attacks on our voting rights keep coming, and they conveniently keep landing on this county where we are rewriting what everybody thought they knew about Texas politics.** It sure seems like the extremists running this state are scared of your vote, because Texas runs a database just fine when it wants to. They handed Trump's Justice Department the personal data of 18.4 million voters without losing a single record, birthdays and license numbers and partial Socials included. They ran our rolls through his citizenship screening right on schedule. **_The only job they keep botching is the one that gets and keeps you registered._** [**Chip in and help us out-organize every fumble they throw at us.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt8x-iH89nEL443ae5ECbr-Th9FyfqbKymXOK6gpzdaMrInEn42061KYByqE08TmVvH4XqHA1JlTQxgVwn1d-ERVbBkxq00p-8emLAmplSK5hRVx_N0NYdp80vzHTw6go2E0TV_96NHKJ2JA8v93e6WkdI7Bs8VTO8BexRzP8BuxMtdPF9kQtLE_eiyfwMxK6iFiPx1stgrPZIY5RdH8uXpiik5r-JWugkJLNJdzwFwgGduK87T4pt5jrSWiKmufJwTMXnMchHBkPwJgyT8nn_yZl7Sdt-VXJb2B8R9uHy9WCA_aH9uIX-RueHs1JFSSxLF4nATBj2vKvUCBX4kWrrIwAtVZGIsp0IWNVOwP8v-a-Ncht9ahFEQ7OBmq9M5qlsdA/4uc/X3ZsUopoTiCf-zBPoW_BfQ/h2/h001.my-OPtv9S9Sq-hAD8wtsEpm5xxiFk1KRr3cTpI9MeAI) I flew combat missions for this country because I believe in self-government and the right of every citizen to shape it through their vote. Defending that right did not stop being my job when I hung up the uniform. It became this campaign. So here is your two-minute mission. [Check your registration at the Secretary of State's website today](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.xqm-apKpWqGuZCDDu9wrxeSKMV_aQzHCph-4ck3d1aAhx04cEc8_mdYe60rqX2s06gt3AbNwPf5ibuBAVlsJBOGqqPbHe4IYo52TXzHf98yVCaoh3ZYv-u1vm4_ylmQdRLxrGX0ysXLL6uQvgdzy2iYlSWDUCoCBeMFeuOMZ_-vSq2585u25_7mPlliK-pJySPuMbJYK4KlIeKlPdL115ELsXthEX8xbWGhXvfEBJfc9EGsw56ASHIqI1BxdlJfp7p21I9YL7elkKIghKaGwxl1ufq6lm_wiafEnjiCqAU4Ye9wejMED-Urk8ch3tCCSautM4cXKuCx_qwTNPd7IPhGdNScLo1mNUDSj_O0QwtmlJOVZP4sOffrCXJwulD-8MvwiOX7JjBzPHFn6uu0KuA/4uc/X3ZsUopoTiCf-zBPoW_BfQ/h3/h001.RvHdUGdrQY31-UEb18U1-8s1PLDNJD88mRCndz_8Cwg), especially if you registered or changed your address through DPS. I'm the Democrat running to end it. And I'm emailing you, wherever you live, because this seat just became a national one.

subject: 4 Justice Democrats put their bodies on the line in NYC
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Yesterday, four Justice Democrats took to the streets of New York City to
protest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s visit to the United
Nations headquarters.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260925.RooW8W&refcode=em20260925-38292&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=38292%2E1203867%2E3JH6g4 ]Group of protesters holding banners and all wearing white shirts that
say "Fund People Not Bombs"; (L-R) Darializa Avila Chevalier, Melat Kiros,
Chris Rabb, Dr. Adam Hamawy sit at the front of the group

Darializa Avila Chevalier, Melat Kiros, Chris Rabb, and Dr. Adam Hamawy
put their bodies on the line alongside more than 400 others at a mass
anti-war sit-in organized by Jewish Voice for Peace.

While international war criminal Netanyahu was free to give a boastful,
threatening speech inside the UN, Dari was one of about 100 protesters who
were zip-tied and arrested simply for speaking out against war and
genocide.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260925.RooW8W&refcode=em20260925-38292&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=38292%2E1203867%2E3JH6g4 ]Post on X from @DarializaforNY: "As the Democratic Nominee for New
York's 13th Congressional District, I refuse to allow a war criminal to
roam the streets of our city unchallenged. I refuse to be complicit in
genocide."; attached are two images of Darializa at the protest, the one
on the left is of her actively protesting, the right image is her being
zip-tied

Together, these Justice Democrats joined a broad coalition of people from
all walks of life — Jewish, Palestinian, Iranian, and Lebanese Americans
along with veterans, descendants of Holocaust survivors, young people,
grandmothers, rabbis, elected officials, actors, and comedians — to demand
an end to Israel’s genocide in Gaza and stop U.S. military funding to
Israel.

And thanks to people like you,
Peter, Dari, Melat, Chris, and
Dr. Adam will continue this fight in Congress come January, where they
will vote to block the bombs, end the terror Israel is inflicting on
people in Gaza, the West Bank, and Lebanon, and stop using U.S. taxpayer
dollars to enable it.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260925.RooW8W&refcode=em20260925-38292&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1004&akid=38292%2E1203867%2E3JH6g4 ]We can send three more champions for peace and justice to Washington
next year, but we need your support to get them over the finish line in
this November’s midterm elections. Will you pitch in $5
before Wednesday’s final end-of-quarter deadline to help us elect three
more Justice Dems to Congress?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260925.RooW8W&refcode=em20260925-38292&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1023&akid=38292%2E1203867%2E3JH6g4 ]Contribute $5

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

Contribute to Justice Democrats: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/justicedemocrats?refcode=em20260925-38292-footer&t=1024&refcode2=38292_1203867_3JH6g4&akid=38292%2E1203867%2E3JH6g4

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way for us to reach you about opportunities to get involved. If you need to remove yourself from our email list, click here to unsubscribe: https://go.justicedemocrats.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=1025&akid=38292%2E1203867%2E3JH6g4

[William Turton](https://substack.com/redirect/3a6536ed-327c-4777-adb2-dd13d51f771c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is the Pro Publica investigative reporter who released a report this week alleging that Sen. Susan Collins and several members of her staff engaged in an elaborate conspiracy to funnel defense appropriations money into a federal contractor in return for campaign contributions. He joins us on _The Robinson Report_ to talk about the credibility of his primary source for the story -- convicted fraudster and serial liar Martin Kao -- as well as what readers are to make of the Federal Elections Commission and the FBI under Joe Biden dropping the case. Turton defends his report and insists sources he communicated with attested to the credibility of both Kao and unnamed FBI agents familiar with the probe.

Peter, Childcare is breaking the backs of working families. It’s too expensive for parents. Childcare workers aren’t paid enough. And millions of families are forced to make impossible choices between working, paying the bills, and caring for their kids. This isn’t the American dream we were promised. And we can fix this. **Today, I introduced the **[**Free Child Care for America Act**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139975952/649117803/252269772?id=136731278&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDMyMDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMWY4YWJkMzQtMmFiOS1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ejqP0Np2HR9fBunhIIx4Glxz6Fj1jZQYz4KPJjx9D3E=&emci=1e8abd34-2ab9-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=1f8abd34-2ab9-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=9848080)**— a nearly $1 trillion, 10-year plan to build a universal childcare system in America.** Here’s what it would do: ✅ Make childcare free for eligible families✅ Give parents real choices—whether they want a childcare center, care from family or friends, or to stay home with their young children ✅ Expand the supply of childcare so families can actually find care when they need it✅ Support childcare providers with funding to cover operating costs ✅ Raise pay for childcare workers **[ADD YOUR NAME: Tell Congress to pass the Free Child Care for America Act.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139975953/649117804/525029872?contactdata=7q3LSMuSdoQHdQpfamX1cR0RIm6C1AFzb9jPjhDLUercmEDPzpOGF0bNqX440+Lw62hc4YzzQO8LccWTNDRRqDqGAGqiLCR70X1iWwRPfvSTwSucMhvCCcc4ZB1BgvFV2sF//JtasEc4VUirobJPYP8Ez8mSLS7HIvkhmtVzUyyQrJ5jbE2tKP8F4CCB2iPb&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDMyMDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMWY4YWJkMzQtMmFiOS1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ejqP0Np2HR9fBunhIIx4Glxz6Fj1jZQYz4KPJjx9D3E=&emci=1e8abd34-2ab9-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=1f8abd34-2ab9-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=9848080)**

Yes, this is a major undertaking. But if we’re serious about solving this crisis, we have to be serious about investing in it. We can pay for it by making different choices. **End the war in Iran. Tax billionaires. Cut wasteful Pentagon spending. Invest that money in American families instead.** That’s economic patriotism. For too long, Washington has told working families to fix their own problems while handing billions in tax breaks and subsidies to corporations and billionaires. It’s time to shift our priorities. We should make it possible for parents to work and raise their kids. We should make sure childcare workers can earn a decent living. clean_body: I’m introducing a comprehensive plan to build a universal childcare system.| | | | Peter, Childcare is breaking the backs of working families. It’s too expensive for parents. Childcare workers aren’t paid enough. And millions of families are forced to make impossible choices between working, paying the bills, and caring for their kids. This isn’t the American dream we were promised. And we can fix this. Today, I introduced the — a nearly $1 trillion, 10-year plan to build a universal childcare system in America. Here’s what it would do: ✅ Make childcare free for eligible families✅ Give parents real choices—whether they want a childcare center, care from family or friends, or to stay home with their young children ✅ Expand the supply of childcare so families can actually find care when they need it✅ Support childcare providers with funding to cover operating costs ✅ Raise pay for childcare workers Yes, this is a major undertaking. But if we’re serious about solving this crisis, we have to be serious about investing in it. We can pay for it by making different choices. End the war in Iran. Tax billionaires. Cut wasteful Pentagon spending. Invest that money in American families instead. That’s economic patriotism. For too long, Washington has told working families to fix their own problems while handing billions in tax breaks and subsidies to corporations and billionaires. It’s time to shift our priorities. We should make it possible for parents to work and raise their kids. We should make sure childcare workers can earn a decent living. And we should build an economy where having children doesn't mean putting your future at risk. We don't have to accept an economy that leaves working families behind. We can build one that works for them. Thank you for your activism and all that you do. Onward, Ro | | | | | | | Wait! One more thing– Ro doesn't accept a cent from lobbyists or PACs, meaning our work is completely funded by grassroots supporters like you. By donating just $3 today, you’re helping us create a country that works for everyone, not just those at the top. That means a renewed investment in American manufacturing, Medicare for All, student debt relief, and a green future. # Some Thoughts from Virginia McIntyre for Absentee Ballot Voters
A New Voice for New York’s 25th District Dear Neighbor, I hope you have received my previous emails. Due to the partisan divide and the constant ads—with each side blaming the other for our problems while neither side is finding solutions—most people are exhausted by all of it. I have approached this campaign with an entirely different spirit. I am running to represent everyone in our community, no matter their ethnic background, religion, or party affiliation. I know that beyond all the political noise, we share similar concerns. We all feel that our energy bills are too high, healthcare is too expensive, and the cost of living has increased faster than our paychecks. Political division has made people feel frustrated, isolated, and unsure that their votes even matter. I am running for Congress to do something different. I am a Republican, but I believe the will of the people should matter more than party affiliation. Big PAC donors should not influence the decisions of our representatives, and I have refused PAC donations because I am looking to work for you—not the political machine. |
## Based on community feedback, I have pledged to:
✓ Support term limits for members of Congress ✓ Co-sponsor and support the No Bonuses for Utility Executives Act ✓ Co-sponsor and support the Keep the Lights Local Act ✓ Fight to reduce the cost of healthcare and utilities ✓ Strengthen education and career opportunities ✓ Actively engage with our community ✓ Work across party lines to deliver results
